# implement.py parent: terminal blockers still gate topological readiness

relocated-from:AH-0MVL5B7C80000MT6 (AI_Hell worklog), moved to this repo because `implement.py` is agent-infrastructure code owned by SorraAgents (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`).

discovered-from:AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent` builds its dependency graph from **every** in-chain
dependency edge, including edges whose blocker is already terminal, so a
finished blocker still occupies the topological ordering and delays — or in
practice starves — the genuinely ready child that depends on it. A child whose
blockers are all terminal is *ready now*, yet it can be sorted behind unrelated
children purely because its (finished) blocker had a high `sortIndex`.

## Users

- **Primary — agent/operator running an epic:** "As the agent driving an epic
  with `implement.py parent`, I want a child whose blockers are all already
  finished to be selected as soon as it is the lowest-sorting ready child, so
  in-flight implementation work is never skipped and I never have to finish it
  manually."
- **Secondary — producer/reviewer:** "As a producer, I want the reported
  implementation order to mean 'blockers first, then sortIndex', so I can
  predict which child the next run will start."
- **Maintainer:** "As a maintainer, I want the ordering fix covered by a
  regression test with the exact shape that broke, so the readiness rule
  cannot silently regress."

## Observed failure (2026-10-23, epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S)

Resolved order for the epic's 8 children:

`[TOOK(test-failure, done), 3X5M, MVIS(done), VDA9, 7NGZ, O53Z(done), K0V4, BAAN]`

`K0V4` (sortIndex 3000 — the *lowest* open child) has an outbound `depends-on`
edge to `O53Z` (its test-first contract child, sortIndex 8100). `O53Z` was
already `completed`, so `K0V4` should have been ready immediately; instead it
was released only after `O53Z`'s slot near the end of the queue.

Consequences:

1. `implement.py parent AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S` never reached `K0V4` although its
   worktree held a completed in-flight implementation — it returned
   "start child VDA9"; the in-flight work had to be finished manually with
   `implement.py finish K0V4`.
2. The reported order is not "blockers first" in any intuitive sense: a ready
   child was deferred behind unrelated children purely because its finished
   blocker sorted late.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Terminal blockers never gate readiness.** In
   `_resolve_implementation_order()` an in-chain dependency edge whose blocker
   is terminal — `_is_terminal_child()` is true: status in `TERMINAL_STATUSES`
   (`in_review`, `completed`, `done`, `deleted`) or the item is soft-deleted —
   contributes neither to `in_degree[child]` nor to `dependents[blocker]`. The
   graph is therefore built over non-terminal children only, and a child whose
   in-chain blockers are all terminal is in the **initial** ready set.
2. **Ready children are ordered by their own `(sortIndex, id)`.** For the
   reproduction shape (open child `LOW` with sortIndex 3000 whose only in-chain
   blocker is a `completed` child `HIGH` with sortIndex 8100, plus an unrelated
   open child `MID` with sortIndex 5000) the resolved order starts with `LOW`,
   then `MID`, then `HIGH` — i.e. `LOW`'s position is decided by its own
   `sortIndex`, never by its blocker's.
3. **Regression test reproduces the exact shape.** A new
   `skill/implement/tests/test_resolve_implementation_order.py` covers at
   minimum: (a) the reproduction shape above, asserting `LOW` is **first**;
   (b) an all-terminal children set, asserting ordering is purely
   `(sortIndex, id)`; (c) a non-terminal chain `A ← B` (both open), asserting
   `A` precedes `B` (real blocking still respected); (d) a soft-deleted blocker
   treated as terminal; (e) an external blocker (id not among the children)
   creating no edge; (f) the existing cycle path still returning
   `([], error)` with the cyclic children named; (g) `_next_child_to_implement`
   still refusing a child whose in-chain blocker is **non**-terminal. The
   reproduction test must be shown red against the pre-fix source and green
   after the fix.
4. **No change to adjacent behaviour.** Cycle detection (fail-fast, no infinite
   recursion), cross-project/external-blocker reporting, `_classify_child`
   (`skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress`) and the blocked-child guard in
   `_next_child_to_implement` are unchanged, and the parent still advances once
   every child is terminal.
5. **Documentation updated.** The
   `_resolve_implementation_order()` docstring states the readiness rule
   (terminal blockers are pre-satisfied), and the parent-recursion/dependency
   ordering text in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (plus any `docs/dev/*` reference
   that describes the ordering) is updated to match; code comments explain why
   terminal edges are excluded.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** — the
   implement-skill group (`pytest -q skill/implement/tests/`) is green and the
   full suite (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full`) passes on the
   committed tip.

## Constraints

- **Repository ownership.** The code is agent infrastructure owned by **SorraAgents**:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `SorraAgents/skill`; the AI_Hell checkout contains no `skill/` tree). The item
  was relocated here from the AI_Hell worklog (AH-0MVL5B7C80000MT6) by producer
  decision, following the SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 precedent, while keeping its
  `discovered-from` link to the AI_Hell epic that exposed the defect. The change,
  its tests, docs, commit and full-suite evidence therefore all stay inside this
  repo — `implement.py start <id>` from this checkout creates the worktree here
  and `wl` resolves this store, so no cross-store resolution is involved.
- **Explicit authorisation to edit `skill/`.** The repository-boundary rule
  forbids editing `skill/` unless explicitly instructed; this work item *is*
  that instruction, scoped to the files listed under **Key Files**.
- **Determinism preserved.** Tie-break stays `(sortIndex, id)`; no
  non-deterministic iteration order (sets are always sorted before use).
- **Narrow scope.** Do **not** change `wl dep` semantics, `sortIndex`
  generation/assignment, child classification, or the `parent` phase's broader
  control flow.
- **No new runtime dependencies;** Python 3.8+ compatible; stdlib only (as the
  existing module is).

## Existing state

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:

- `TERMINAL_STATUSES = {"in_review", "completed", "done", "deleted"}` (~line
  769), `_is_terminal_status()` (~772), `_is_terminal_child()` (~784, also
  treats a soft-deleted `deletedBy` child as terminal).
- `_classify_child()` (~810) — `skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress` /
  `implement`.
- `_resolve_implementation_order(children, blockers)` (~836) — Kahn's
  algorithm; today:

  ```python
  for edge in blockers.get(cid, []):
      bid = str(edge.get("id", ""))
      if bid in child_ids:              # <-- terminal blockers still counted
          in_degree[cid] += 1
          dependents[bid].append(cid)
  ```

  The ready queue is `sorted(... in_degree[cid] == 0 ..., key=(sortIndex, id))`
  and is re-sorted after each release, so a terminal blocker with a high
  `sortIndex` delays its dependent.
- `_next_child_to_implement(children, blockers_map)` (~905) already gates on
  *non-terminal* in-chain blockers (`all(bid in terminal_ids ...)`), so the
  guard and the sort currently disagree — the inconsistency this item fixes.
- Caller `phase_parent` (~5124) calls `_resolve_implementation_order()` and
  returns early on a cycle error; `_next_child_to_implement()` then picks from
  the ordered list.
- Tests live in `skill/implement/tests/` (6 files, `.pi/test-config.json` group
  `implement` → `pytest -q skill/implement/tests/`); **no test currently covers
  `_resolve_implementation_order` or `_next_child_to_implement` directly.**

## Desired change

- Skip terminal blockers when building the graph in
  `_resolve_implementation_order()` — e.g.

  ```python
  if bid in child_ids and not _is_terminal_child(child_by_id[bid]):
      in_degree[cid] += 1
      dependents[bid].append(cid)
  ```

  (equivalently: collapse terminal children out of the graph before the sort).
  Terminal children remain present in the returned order so the caller still
  reports/finishes them, and their own placement is still decided by their own
  `(sortIndex, id)`.
- Cycle detection then operates over the non-terminal subgraph only; keep the
  same error message/format and the fail-fast return.
- Update the docstring (readiness rule + why terminal edges are excluded) and
  the ordering documentation in `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.
- Add the regression test module described in AC3.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (SorraAgents) — **Edit**:
  `_resolve_implementation_order()` graph construction + docstring;
  `_next_child_to_implement()` docstring cross-reference if needed.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_resolve_implementation_order.py` (SorraAgents) —
  **New**: ordering/readiness regression tests (AC3), including the red-then-
  green reproduction shape.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (SorraAgents) — **Edit**: parent-recursion /
  dependency-order text states that terminal blockers do not gate readiness.
- `docs/dev/*` in SorraAgents — **Edit (if present)**: any ordering description
  that contradicts the new rule (verify with
  `grep -rn "topological\|dependency order" docs/ skill/implement/`).

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Masking a real cycle.* Excluding terminal blockers from the graph could hide
  a cycle that passes through a terminal child. Mitigation: a cycle can only
  block work that still needs doing, so detection over the non-terminal
  subgraph is the correct semantics; document it in the docstring and cover it
  with AC3(f) (cycle among non-terminal children still fails fast).
- *Accidental behaviour drift elsewhere.* `_next_child_to_implement()` has its
  own terminal-aware guard; the fix must align with it rather than replace it.
  Mitigation: AC3(g) asserts the guard still refuses non-terminal-blocked
  children; AC4 forbids changing adjacent paths.
- *Cross-repo verification gap.* The AI_Hell audit/CI cannot see SorraAgents
  files, so a green AI_Hell report does not prove the fix. Mitigation: run the
  implement-skill pytest group and the SorraAgents full suite from the
  SorraAgents worktree and record the evidence (red/green, commit hash) on this
  item, per AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB.
- *Test-gate selection.* Changed-scope selection may not see the new test file
  until it is tracked; Mitigation: `git add` before the gate run and confirm the
  `implement` group is selected (otherwise fall back to full scope).
- *Scope creep.* The 2026-10-23 report also notes the confusing reported order
  generally and the manual `finish K0V4` step; richer ordering diagnostics or
  `parent`-phase rework are **not** in scope. Mitigation: record follow-ups as
  separate items (see Related work) rather than widening this fix.

**Assumptions**

- The item now lives in the **SorraAgents** worklog (relocated from AI_Hell by
  producer decision, per the SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 precedent); the AI_Hell epic
  AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S remains recorded as the origin via `discovered-from`.
- Terminal blockers are pre-satisfied for *ordering* purposes but are still
  reported in the resolved order (existing `skip-terminal` classification
  handles them in the loop), so no caller contract changes.
- Soft-deleted children behave as terminal for this rule (they can never be
  implemented) — consistent with `_is_terminal_child()`.

## Related work

Cross-repo (SorraAgents — the code's owning repo; automated `find-related`
searched only the AI_Hell store because the item's prefix pins that store, and
its file matches are noise here):

- **SA-0MSQIJBTB008RHS1** — *completed* — V2: Dependency-graph resolution,
  topological ordering & cycle detection; the change that introduced
  `_resolve_implementation_order()`.
- **SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T** — *completed* — implement skill: `/skill:implement
  <parent-id>` must automatically implement children and blockers in the chain;
  defined the in-chain/external blocker split and the blocked-child guard.
- **SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876** — *open* — implement.py parent ignores the
  do-not-delegate tag when selecting the next child; same selection path
  (`_next_child_to_implement`), different rule. **Relocated** from the AI_Hell
  worklog because `implement.py` is SorraAgents-owned — the precedent for the
  OPEN QUESTION below.
- **SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9** — *completed* — implement skill: drive all epic
  children to completion (fresh session per child); the `parent`/`drive` flow
  that consumes this ordering.

AI_Hell (origin store — historical, retained for traceability after the relocation):

- **AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S** — Create an improved Phase Shift effect — the epic
  whose run exposed the defect (`discovered-from`).
- **AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB** — ship skill kebab-case fix — *completed* — the
  cross-repo precedent: AI_Hell item, SorraAgents commit, cross-repo evidence
  recorded on the item.
- **AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ** — run-release Discord notification wiring — the
  earlier cross-repo precedent referenced by the above.
- **AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81** — implement.py: behind-only child worktree
  mis-detected as "has changes" and auto-finished — *open* — sibling defect in
  the same `parent`/`finish` machinery (no fix overlap).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was held: the seed context (problem statement,
observed impact, expected behaviour, suggested fix and ACs) was sufficient to
draft an actionable brief, and the repo research below answered the remaining
implementation questions.

- **Q1 — Which repository owns the code, and where does the fix land?**
  — Answer (repo research + precedent, not a producer question):
  **SorraAgents**. `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `SorraAgents/skill`; the AI_Hell checkout has no `skill/` tree
  (`find / -name implement.py` → `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`,
  identical to the installed copy, `diff` clean). Precedent
  **AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB** (AI_Hell item, commit `4be04fa7a` on SorraAgents
  `dev`, cross-repo evidence in a comment) and **AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ**. Source:
  `git log --grep="AH-"` in SorraAgents; comment on AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB.
- **Q2 — Does `implement.py` work at all against a foreign worklog store?**
  — Answer (repo research): yes. `implement.py` routes every `wl` call through
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags()`, whose
  prefix-to-sibling scan maps an `AH-…` id to `AI_Hell/.worklog` even when cwd
  is SorraAgents, so `implement.py start AH-0MVL5B7C80000MT6` from the SorraAgents
  checkout yields a SorraAgents worktree + AI_Hell worklog. Source:
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (~lines 290–370).
- **Q3 — How should terminal be defined for the readiness rule?**
  — Answer (repo research): reuse `_is_terminal_child()` (statuses
  `in_review`/`completed`/`done`/`deleted` plus soft-deleted), matching the
  guard already used by `_next_child_to_implement()`. Source:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (~769–808, ~905–955).
- **Q4 — Is there an existing test to extend?**
  — Answer (repo research): no. `skill/implement/tests/` has 6 modules and none
  imports `_resolve_implementation_order` / `_next_child_to_implement`
  (`grep -rn` clean), so AC3 creates a new module covered by the existing
  `.pi/test-config.json` `implement` group. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q5 — Should this item be relocated to the SorraAgents worklog?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **yes — recreate it on
  `../SorraAgents`, `wl sync`, and delete the AI_Hell item when done.**
  Rationale/precedent: `implement.py` is agent-infrastructure code owned by
  SorraAgents (SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 was relocated for the same reason), so all
  such items now live in the owning repo; the cross-repo pattern of
  AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB (AI_Hell item, SorraAgents commit, cross-repo evidence
  comment) is superseded for future items. Research: two conflicting precedents
  were found (AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB kept the item in AI_Hell; SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876
  relocated) — the producer resolved in favour of relocation. Source:
  interactive reply + the `relocated-from` note in SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T** – implement skill: /skill:implement <parent-id> must automatically implement children and blockers in the chain (completed)
- **SA-0MVLJXTYY005XQDV** – Reconcile terminal child once finish bound exhausted (blocked)
- **SA-0MVLJWMQ8007EDW0** – Reconcile terminal child after spawn failure (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac3, ac4, acceptance, acs, actionable (+422 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac3, ac4, acceptance, acs, actionable (+399 more)

worklog, so the findings are actioned here instead of blocking another
project's release.

ContentCreator's audit code-quality scan resolved paths from `Key Files`
entries that point outside its own project, so it filed these against
ContentCreator's worklog (epic `OSL-0MVP7C8OT000S61W`). The scan is now bounded
to the audited project (`SA-0MVPDTSRV0049KW2`); these copies are re-filed
here so the findings survive the clean-up.

# plan-if-needed overwrites operator-confirmed effort/risk

Discovered-from: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 (plan session 2026-10-27).

## Problem

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` `plan-if-needed` re-runs the effort-and-risk
estimator whenever no prior `effort_and_risk_skill` comment exists on the item
(`is_effort_risk_computed`), silently overwriting operator-confirmed
effort/risk values with heuristic estimates. On SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 the
operator-confirmed carry-over risk High / effort M was replaced with Extra
Small / Low (comment 09:38:39Z), materially understating risk of a commit-gate
change. The original values were restored manually.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plan-if-needed` never overwrites an explicitly set/human-confirmed
      effort or risk with a heuristic recomputation; the recompute path is gated
      on the absence of a deliberate value (with a recorded rationale), or the
      overwrite is surfaced as an explicit warning/approval.
- [ ] A regression test covers the overwrite scenario (operator value present,
      no prior estimator comment) and asserts the value is preserved.
- [ ] Origin case documented: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 restore comment
      SA-C0MVQKM7XD0089OVQ.
data.title: plan-if-needed overwrites operator-confirmed effort/risk

Discovered during LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 (llm worklog) via test-failure SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ.

## Problem
`tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` spawns `process.env.PYTHON || "python3"` and exercises the real `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, which imports `numpy` (line 117). The repo declares no Python dependency manifest (no `requirements.txt`), so on a bare interpreter the whole unit node suite fails with `transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'` — the failure was red on this host from 2026-10-15 until numpy was installed ad hoc during the item above.

## Goal
As a maintainer, I want the voice-input worker's Python dependencies declared (and/or the unit test to skip with a clear message when they are absent), so a fresh checkout's full suite is green without undocumented host setup.

## Acceptance criteria

## Goal

Users of the refactor skill need to know whether the project's **tests are
worth keeping**, not only whether the source has code smells. Integrate the
`test-churn` skill into the refactor workflow so every refactor run also
produces test-churn metrics (rewrite ratio, test growth, per-area churn), and
surface that evidence in the refactor skill's final report.

## Problem Statement

The refactor skill currently analyses **source code only** (`refactor.py` scans
`.py`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`; tests are scanned for
smells like any other code, but their *value* is never assessed). Test-value
evidence exists but only on demand, via the separate `test-churn` skill
(`skill`-external, script `test_churn_analysis.py`). Nothing in the refactor
workflow detects a suite that is growing without manifest benefit, so the
`refactor` run cannot report the pruning signal documented in the test-churn
skill's pruning review workflow.

## User Stories

- **Agent running a refactor:** "When I run the refactor skill, the report tells
  me whether the test suite is growing without benefit, so I can file a
  pruning work item without remembering to run a second skill."
- **Operator / producer:** "Every refactor report carries reproducible test
  churn numbers, so TDD-ROI evidence is produced continuously rather than
  requested ad hoc."
- **Maintainer:** "The integration is additive — a missing/broken test-churn
  script never fails a refactor run, and `--no-churn` restores today's exact
  behaviour."

## Proposed Behaviour

1. `refactor.py` invokes the test-churn analyser as an **additional pipeline
   stage** after smell detection, for both invocation modes (full scan and
   session boundary).
2. A new `--no-churn` flag skips the stage (mirroring `--no-sync`,
   `--no-linter`, `--no-llm`) for offline/deterministic/fast runs.
3. The **human report** gains a test-churn section showing at minimum: modified
   only rewrite ratio, including-new rewrite ratio, net test lines/files
   growth, and the flagged top-churn areas.
4. The **`--json` report** gains a `test_churn` key carrying the analyser's
   `test_churn_data.json` payload (or a documented failure/omitted marker).
5. The stage is **non-fatal**: an unavailable analyser, non-git directory, or
   analyser error logs a warning and the refactor run continues with unchanged
   exit-code semantics (mirroring the existing `wl sync` policy).
6. `SKILL.md` documents the stage, the flag, the report section and the
   non-fatal policy, and cross-references the test-churn skill.

## Constraint: skill boundary

`skill/refactor/` must not import `test_churn_analysis.py` from the installed
skill directory. The integration must resolve the analyser at runtime (the
documented `$(skill_path test-churn)` pattern) or invoke it as a subprocess, so
this repo stays the canonical source and no copy of the analyser is vendored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A full-project `/skill:refactor` run renders a test-churn section in the human report containing the modified-only rewrite ratio, the including-new rewrite ratio, and net test line growth.
- [ ] AC2: `refactor.py --json` emits a `test_churn` key whose value contains the analyser metrics (at minimum the two rewrite ratios and `growth_metrics`).
- [ ] AC3: `--no-churn` skips the stage and produces a report byte-identical to current behaviour (no test-churn section, no `test_churn` key).
- [ ] AC4: When the analyser is unavailable or returns non-zero, the run logs a warning, completes successfully, and reports the stage as unavailable — the refactor exit code is unchanged.
- [ ] AC5: `session boundary` mode (`refactor.py <work-item-id>`) also runs the stage, and its work-item `StatusLifecycle` behaviour is unchanged (item never left `in_progress`).
- [ ] AC6: New tests cover the added stage (report rendering, JSON key, `--no-churn`, and the non-fatal failure path) without shelling out to the real analyser — following the test-writing guidelines (no source-grep or self-referential tests).
- [ ] AC7: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` documents the stage, flag, report section, non-fatal policy and the cross-reference to the test-churn skill.
- [ ] AC8: No code under `skill/refactor/` imports from an installed skill path; the analyser is resolved at runtime or invoked as a subprocess.
- [ ] AC9: Full suite passes (run via the test skill).
data.title: Integrate test-churn analysis into the refactor skill and report

## Goal

Make the project's test suite **earn its runtime**: every remaining test should
pin observable behaviour, and no test should exist that cannot fail for a
reason a developer cares about. This epic covers a complete, evidence-led
test-value refactor of the suite — measure, classify, prune, rework, and guard
against reintroduction — rather than the current one-file-at-a-time ad-hoc
cleanups.

## Problem Statement

The suite has grown substantially and carries demonstrable waste:

- **Measured growth (test-churn analyser v2.1.0, `dev` @ 7875214):**
  208,809 test lines added vs 71,787 deleted → **net +137,022 lines**;
  498 test files added vs 114 deleted → **net +384 files**. Net growth is
  positive in **every** calendar quarter, accelerating in 2026-Q3 (+55,892)
  and 2026-Q4 (+38,024).
- **Rewrite ratio is LOW** (14.0% modified-only, 6.2% including new files),
  which means tests largely *survive* feature evolution. That is good news for
  TDD value, but it means growth is dominated by **additive accumulation**,
  not churn — precisely the pattern where dead, duplicated and
  source-grep/structural tests survive unnoticed because nothing forces them
  to be re-examined.
- **Known confirmed offenders found so far:** 5 source-grep / structural
  anti-pattern tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
  (SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23); 15 test helpers invoking real `git` non-hermetically
  (already tracked, SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0).
- There is **no standing mechanism** that classifies test files by value, so
  every finding so far depended on a human/agent choosing to look.

## Why an epic (not another leaf)

Value assessment is a repeatable pipeline — detect candidates, prove they no
longer map to behaviour, prune or rework, verify nothing broke, and prevent
reintroduction. That needs coordinated child items across measurement,
classification, remediation, and guarding; single-file items cannot deliver it.

## Existing related work — do NOT duplicate

These items already exist and must be **depended on / coordinated with**, not
recreated:

- `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23` — rework the 5 source-grep tests in `test-check-audit-gate.mjs`.
- `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0` — migrate 15 raw-git test helpers to `git_sandbox` (hermeticity, not value).
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — integrate test-churn metrics into the refactor skill.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (evidence arm).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.
- `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU` — scheduled test-churn runs across projects.

## Scope

1. **Measure (baseline).** Capture the test-churn baseline (rewrite ratios, net
   growth, per-area churn, suite wall-clock runtime, per-file runtime) so every
   later change is provable.
2. **Classify.** Run the code-path evaluator (`skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`)
   plus the `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-pattern checklist
   over the whole suite, recording a **keep / rework / prune** verdict per file.
3. **Prove.** For each prune candidate, demonstrate the behaviour it pins is
   either not observable, already covered elsewhere, or no longer exists
   (`git blame` + coverage grep of the public API). Mutation testing is the
   tie-breaker where provenance is unclear.
4. **Remediate.** Prune dead/duplicate tests; rework devalued ones (source-grep
   → behaviour; placeholder → real assertion or delete; simulation → exercise
   production code).
5. **Guard.** Add a regression guard so the pruned anti-pattern classes cannot
   be reintroduced silently, and so future additions are screened.
6. **Report.** Record before/after metrics so the value delivered is auditable.

## Non-goals

- Not a coverage-maximisation exercise: reducing test count is acceptable and
  expected where tests pin nothing.
- Not a rewrite of the audit/refactor/implement skills' behaviour.
- Not the hermeticity migration (tracked separately in `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A baseline is recorded in this item: modified-only and including-new rewrite ratios, net test file/line growth, suite wall-clock runtime, and the evaluator/checklist verdict for every test file in scope.
- [ ] AC2: Every test file in scope carries an explicit keep / rework / prune verdict with its justifying evidence, and the totals reconcile (verdicts sum to files in scope).
- [ ] AC3: Every prune candidate has written evidence that the behaviour it pinned is not observable, already covered via the public API, or gone — no test is deleted on suspicion alone.
- [ ] AC4: All `prune`-verdict tests are removed and all `rework`-verdict tests are converted to observable-behaviour assertions; no remaining test file reads a source/markdown file and asserts on its text.
- [ ] AC5: After the refactor, `evaluate_usefulness.py` reports no `remove` verdict for any scanned test file, and the suite contains zero placeholder or zero-assertion tests.
- [ ] AC6: The suite is green (full scope, run via the test skill) and no acceptance criterion of any work item loses coverage — demonstrated by the audits and a before/after coverage map, not by assertion counts.
- [ ] AC7: Suite wall-clock runtime is measurably reduced (or, where runtime rises, the item documents why the surviving tests justify it) with before/after numbers.
- [ ] AC8: A regression guard fails the suite if a newly added test matches a pruned anti-pattern class (source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential simulation), without becoming a source-grep test itself.
- [ ] AC9: The pruning workflow in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` and the anti-patterns in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` are updated with anything this pass learned (new anti-patterns, refined criteria).
- [ ] AC10: Full project test suite passes with the changes, and the final report records the before/after deltas.

## Risks

- **Removing a useful test is a regression; keeping a dead one only costs
  runtime.** Pruning criteria stay conservative — when in doubt, keep the test
  and file a work item.
- Deleting tests can raise apparent coverage drops: coverage is judged by
  behaviour/AC mapping (AC6), never by percentage alone.
- Suite-wide classification is expensive; it must be batched with bounded
  fan-out per the test execution policy (never ad-hoc full suites).

## Notes

Discovered during a test-churn pruning review, 2026-10-28. Priority is medium
because the measured rewrite ratio is already LOW (tests largely survive
feature evolution) — the waste here is accumulation, not thrash, so this is
valuable hygiene rather than an emergency. Children to be created at plan
stage.
data.title: Complete test-value refactor: ensure every test earns its runtime

# plan/intake AC coverage review creates duplicate "Close coverage gap" children when covering children already exist

Discovered-from: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** (tce-main-street) — observed while running `/skill:plan`.

## Problem

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py:apply_coverage_review` (`action: auto_close`) creates one child per *parent AC it judges uncovered*, with the AC text copied verbatim and the title `Close coverage gap: [ ] **ACn — …**`. On a parent whose six feature children each restate an AC in their own words, it judged **all five** ACs uncovered and created five thin `idea`-stage duplicates alongside the real children.

Observed on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`:

- Six properly-formed children existed (config+guard, docs, three AC-verification children, validation) before the review ran.
- `apply_coverage_review(..., target_stage='plan_complete')` returned `action: auto_close` and created `MS-0MVTEXGU6007Z48U`, `MS-0MVTEXH6F008DVJF`, `MS-0MVTEXHK8002E376`, `MS-0MVTEXHWT0074M3M`, `MS-0MVTEXI9G002ROD0` (AC1–AC5).
- A follow-up `run_coverage_review` then reported `coverage_pct: 100` — mapping each parent AC **only** to the newly created gap child, i.e. the review's own output became its evidence.
- Resolution taken: all five were closed as duplicates with a comment mapping each AC to its real covering child, and the parent recorded the outcome.

## Why it matters

- The review silently degrades a well-planned tree (6 children) into 11, half of them AC-text stubs with no key files, constraints or evidence requirement — the opposite of what the review is meant to enforce.
- The "coverage" metric measures lexical similarity between the parent AC text and child AC text, not whether the child actually discharges the AC, so a correctly reworded child scores as a gap.
- Closing the duplicates afterwards leaves the parent at `plan_complete` with the tool's mapping invalidated, so a later re-run is ambiguous (re-create the stubs, or report gaps?).

## Suggested direction

- Before creating a gap child, require a **semantic/structural** match — e.g. child AC coverage by the parent's AC identifier (`AC1`, `AC2`, …, tolerant of reworded text) or by an explicit `Covers: ACn` line in the child description — and skip creation when matched.
- Treat `parent AC -> child` mapping as evidence only when the child has a non-stub body (ACs + Key Files/evidence), and prefer reporting `stop` with the specific unmatched ACs over creating thin children.
- Make the post-`auto_close` mapping exclude the auto-created children themselves when reporting `coverage_pct` (no self-satisfying evidence).
- Cover the case with a test: parent with 5 ACs, 5 reworded covering children → `action: proceed`, no children created.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A parent whose ACs are all covered by existing children — including children that reword the AC text — yields `action: proceed` and creates **zero** children.
- [ ] Gap children are created only when no child declares or demonstrably discharges the AC; the created child still restates the AC verbatim (current behaviour preserved for genuine gaps).
- [ ] `coverage_pct` never counts a gap child created by the same review as coverage for its own AC.
- [ ] Unit test(s) cover: fully-covered-with-reworded-AC → proceed; genuinely uncovered AC → auto_close with exactly one child; idempotent re-run creates no duplicates.
- [ ] `plan`/`intake` SKILL.md text states how coverage is matched, so agents can declare coverage (`Covers: ACn`) instead of relying on wording.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `run_coverage_review`, `apply_coverage_review`, AC extraction/matching.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/plan/SKILL.md`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/intake/SKILL.md` — the documented coverage step.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/tests/` — coverage-review unit tests.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** — the planning session where this was observed (children `MS-0MVTEVJBH003GE8W`, `MS-0MVTEVJRX005N0EA`, `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`, `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`).

## Goal

**As** a project owner scaffolding agent guidance from this repository, **I want** `templates/project-AGENTS.md` to carry the project-level conventions that audits actually enforce, **so that** a new project inherits the two rules that a 2026-10-29 cross-project audit session had to invent on the spot instead of discovering them late.

Discovered-from: `WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V` (ContextHub) — an epic audit that returned `Ready to close: No` on an acceptance criterion the producer had already decided to accept, and an `implement` run whose push gate did not run the suite the skill documentation says it runs.

## Scope note (read before implementing)

The definite "the template" is taken to mean **`templates/project-AGENTS.md`** — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed consumed by `scripts/init_project_agents.py` (see `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md`). That file is deliberately minimal ("reference structure only"), so this item **adds project-level guidance sections, not a copy of the global rules**.

If the intent was instead the framework sources (`skill/audit`, `skill/report`, `skill/implement`) rather than the project template, re-scope this item before implementing — the framework findings are listed at the end as separate, unfiled work.

## Problem

Two conventions were needed during the ContextHub epic and neither is documented for a project owner:

1. **Recording a producer-accepted acceptance-criteria variance.** The producer decided to accept one AC without the last piece of live evidence. The audit runner ignores `wl auditWaiver` entirely (`grep -n waiver skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → no matches); the *only* way to make an audit score that criterion `adjusted` (non-blocking) instead of `partial` (blocking) is to write the accepted variance into the criterion's own text in the work-item description, resolve the recorded open question, and *additionally* record `wl audit-waive` so the closure guard and `wl doctor audit-gaps` agree. Done that way, the epic audit returned `Ready to close: Yes` with the criterion `adjusted`, a clean Phase 1/Phase 2 (`calls=2 parse_ok=2`). Done any other way it silently stays blocking and the item ping-pongs between implement and audit.
2. **Declaring the project's real push gate.** `skill/implement` and `skill/audit` both state that the dev-push pre-push hook enforces the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full`). That is true only where the v3 hook is installed: this repository ships `.githooks/pre-push` (v3, with the scope-aware test gate), but a project seeded earlier (ContextHub) still runs `worklog:pre-push-hook:v2`, which enforces branch policy, the context budget and worklog sync **and nothing else**. Green test evidence therefore came from the `implement.py finish` full-scope run, not the hook. A project owner needs to be told to assert this, because the failure mode is silent: pushes succeed and the cached full-suite evidence the audit consumes read-only never exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `templates/project-AGENTS.md` gains a `## Recording an accepted acceptance-criteria variance` section stating the three-step procedure — (a) amend the criterion's text in the work-item description with an explicit "Accepted variance (producer decision, <date>)" clause naming what evidence stands in for the missing evidence, (b) resolve the corresponding open question in the item description, (c) record `wl audit-waive <id> --reason "<why>"` — and explains **why** the description is mandatory (the audit runner scores an AC from its text and ignores `auditWaiver`).
- AC2: The same template gains a `## Declaring your push gate` section telling a project owner to verify which pre-push hook version the project actually runs (`git config core.hooksPath` + the `worklog:pre-push-hook:vN` banner line) and to record the answer in the project's own guidance, so the full-suite evidence an audit consumes is known to exist (or is known to come from `implement.py finish` instead of the hook).
- AC3: `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` is updated to match — it must describe the template as carrying these two optional guidance sections and stay truthful about the "reference structure only, never a copy of the global rules" constraint; `scripts/init_project_agents.py` output must remain idempotent (re-running never duplicates the reference or the new sections).
- AC4: A test pins the guarantee: emitting a fresh project `AGENTS.md` via `scripts/init_project_agents.py` produces a file containing both new sections, and re-running it is a no-op (`scripts/init_project_agents.py --dry-run --json` reports no change).
- AC5: The two conventions stay project-scoped: no global workflow rule is duplicated into the template (the global layer remains `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`), and `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is re-measured only if the template changes the always-loaded surface.
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Key Files

- `templates/project-AGENTS.md` — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed; the two new sections go here.
- `scripts/init_project_agents.py` — the installer that reads the template (`TEMPLATE_PATH`) and must stay idempotent.
- `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` — the installer documentation to keep in sync (it quotes the canonical file verbatim, so the quoted block must be updated too).
- `tests/` — wherever the installer's tests live (`grep -rln "init_project_agents" tests/`), for the AC4 pin.

## Constraints

- Do **not** copy global agent rules (workflow, wl lifecycle, coding disciplines) into the template — that duplication was removed by `SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G` and must not come back.
- Project-specific guidance stays project-specific: both new sections are conventions a *project owner* opts into, not new global mandates.
- Keep the installer idempotent and its output deterministic; no new dependency.
- UK English; match the existing Markdown style of the file and its quoted copy in the docs.

## Related findings from the same session (not in this item's scope — file separately if wanted)

1. `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` maps an AC verdict of `adjusted` to `unmet` in its Acceptance Criteria table (it only knows `met`/`unmet`), so a *passing* audit that carries an accepted variance renders as `❌ failed` with an `unmet` row. The report had to be corrected by hand.
2. `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py start` fails (`ERROR: Failed to create worktree …`) when a feature branch with the expected name still exists but its worktree directory was removed; the operator has to `git worktree add <path> <branch>` manually and re-run `start` (which then resumes idempotently).
3. `skill/audit` in-main-slot mode (default) emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` child screens that, when unserviced, produce a `Ready to close: No` whose AC rows are all `partial` **and** persist partial child audits that later block the parent — `--no-child-in-main-slot` was the only path that produced a usable report in three consecutive runs.
data.title: Carry the accepted-variance and push-gate conventions into templates/project-AGENTS.md

# Refactor: replace the `# noqa: F811` suppressions with one explicit fixture re-export in `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`

## Impact

A reviewer or future test author reading `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` sees the fixture-sharing intent stated **once, at the import**, instead of re-justifying 36 per-line `# noqa: F811` comments at every use site.

## Problem statement

The refactor scan filed this item as a critical `unused_import` finding (ruff `F811`, "Redefinition of unused `implement_mod`") against a worktree copy of `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`. That finding was silenced in commit `c39cb4454` by adding line-scoped `# noqa: F811` comments. Since then the drive-recovery epics grew the file, so **the suppression count is now 36, not the five the intake brief recorded** (corrected below; verified by `grep -c "noqa: F811"` = 36 on `675bdc833d`).

What remains is the suppression noise itself: 36 independent "this is not a redefinition" assertions, each attached to a different use site, when the intent belongs at exactly one place — the import. One explicit re-export at the import site (`implement_mod as implement_mod`) expresses that intent once and removes all 36.

## Users

- **Test maintainer / agent** editing `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`: wants the fixture-sharing intent stated once, at the import.
- **Code reviewer / audit agent**: wants the lint result clean without 36 per-line suppressions to re-justify.
- **Future test author** borrowing another test module's fixture: wants a precedent in this repo for re-exporting a fixture cleanly.

User stories:

- As a test maintainer, I want the fixture re-export declared once at the import so that the 36 `# noqa: F811` comments can be deleted without ruff complaining.
- As a reviewer, I want the file's lint result to stay exactly as clean as its pre-change baseline, so trust in the lint gate is preserved.
- As a future test author, I want a documented pattern for reusing a fixture defined in another test module.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The fixture re-export is declared as its own aliased import — `implement_mod as implement_mod` — and the file contains **zero** `# noqa: F811` comments (down from 36).
   *Verify:* `grep -c "noqa: F811" tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` → `0`; `grep -n "implement_mod as implement_mod" tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` → the aliased import line; `grep -c "noqa: PLC0414" tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` → `1` (the single reason-carrying suppression at that import — see **D1**).
2. The lint gate reports **no new findings** for this file, which is the strongest form of "zero findings" this environment permits.
   *Verify:* the whole-file baseline before the change is exactly one finding — `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py:2718:17: RUF015` (owned by open item `SA-0MWASVPED005YHI1`, deliberately **out of scope** here). After the change `ruff check tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` must still report **only** that one `RUF015` finding and nothing else, and the rules this item touches must be clean: `ruff check --select F401,F811,PLC0414,I001,RUF100 tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` → `All checks passed!`. The code-review gate's `run_ruff` (`from code_review.scripts.linter_runner import run_ruff`) honours `noqa` (it does not pass `--ignore-noqa`), so a `noqa`-carrying re-export stays clean there too; any finding it reports whose path is this file must be the baseline `RUF015` only.
3. Every existing test in `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` passes **unchanged** (no test-logic edits in this item), proving pytest still resolves the re-exported `implement_mod` fixture at all 36 former suppression sites.
   *Verify:* that module's tests are green in the changed-scope run via `/skill:test` (`run_tests.py`); the module's assertions, test names and counts are identical to the pre-change file.
4. The fixture-sharing intent is documented **in the file**: the re-export carries a comment stating that `x as x` is a deliberate re-export (not a redundant rename) and why the single `# noqa: PLC0414` is required, and the module docstring's existing "reuse the `implement_mod` fixture from `tests/test_implement_drive.py`" note stays accurate.
   *Verify:* the comment is present at the import; the docstring paragraph is unchanged in meaning. No external documentation change is warranted — `grep -rn "noqa: F811" --include="*.md" .` and `grep -rln "implement_mod" --include="*.md" .` both return no matches (verified during planning), so there is no README / docs-site / wiki entry describing this suppression to update.
5. Full project test suite passes with the change.
   *Verify:* the dev-push gate's full-suite run (enforced at push; do not run ad-hoc full suites during implementation).

## Constraints

- **Behaviour-neutral refactor.** Only the import statement and the 36 suppression comments change: no production code, no test logic, no fixture semantics.
- **Prescribed import shape (verified against ruff 0.16.0 in this environment).** Because isort (`I001`) splits `as`-imports into their own statement by default, the alias must be a **second** `from tests.test_implement_drive import (...)` statement, separated from the existing block by a blank line, with the `# noqa: PLC0414` on the aliased line itself. See **Verified approach** for the exact, lint-clean snippet.
- **One suppression is expected, not zero.** `x as x` trips `PLC0414` ("Import alias does not rename original package") in this environment, so the re-export carries exactly one `# noqa: PLC0414` with a reason. Do **not** reintroduce any `# noqa: F811`, and do not silence `PLC0414` file-wide. See **D1** and the non-blocking **Open question O1** (`__all__` alternative).
- **Do not touch the pre-existing `RUF015` site** (line 2718, `[...][0]` slice): it belongs to `SA-0MWASVPED005YHI1`, whose plan is already complete. Touching it would duplicate that item and break AC2's baseline comparison.
- **Do not relocate fixtures** into `tests/conftest.py` or a shared fixtures module — larger blast radius; record as a linked follow-up if worthwhile.
- Keep the diff limited to `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`.
- **Pre-condition (worktree hygiene).** The main checkout is currently dirty with changes unrelated to this item (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` modified; untracked `_fake/` and `tests/test_agents_global_stages.py`). `implement.py start` guards on foreign writes, so the implementer must first triage those per the [recovery playbook](skill/implement/SKILL.md#dirty-main-checkout-recovery-playbook) — **never** stash or delete them without explicit operator permission.

## Verified approach

Current import block (lines 69-79):

```python
# Reuse the existing drive-loop harness pattern verbatim: the scripted parent
# runner, the recording session spawner, the child-report helper and the
# module-under-test fixture all come from ``tests/test_implement_drive.py``.
from tests.test_implement_drive import (
    PARENT,
    RecordingSpawner,
```

```python
# ``F811`` at each of the fixture parameters below.
```

Then delete the trailing `# noqa: F811 …` from all 36 sites, preserving each line's code and indentation and leaving no trailing whitespace (verified: 0 lines with trailing whitespace after removal).

The 36 sites, by kind (verified against `675bdc833d`):

| Kind | Count | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| Fixture definitions (`drive_harness`, `recording_reset`) | 2 | 371, 1800 |
| Single-line test signatures (`def test_…(self, implement_mod):`) | 6 | 1300, 2565, 2579, 2587, 2602, 2634 |

Three textual forms are present today: `# noqa: F811` (10 sites), `# noqa: F811 — fixture param` (25 sites), and `# noqa: F811 — fixture param, not a redefinition` (1 site). All 36 sit at end-of-line, so removal never comments out code (verified: AST still parses; changed-line count == 36).

- **A2 — priority.** `low` is right: cosmetic, no functional impact (already set on the item).
- **A3 — ruff version drift.** The `PLC0414` behaviour is specific to this environment's ruff 0.16.0 default rule set. If CI's ruff has a narrower default set, the `PLC0414` noqa becomes unnecessary — and `RUF100` ("unused `noqa` directive") would then flag it. ## Goal

As an agent running the changed-scope test gate, I want a changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file to select the node suite for that directory, so a JS/TS test edit is actually executed before commit instead of only at the push-time full suite.

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_is_test_file()` recognises `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `*.test.mjs` and `*_test.mjs` but **not** the repo's dominant node convention `test-*.mjs`. Consequences:

1. A changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file is not classified as a test file, so `map_changed_to_tests()` tries the convention mapping instead (`test_<stem>.py` etc.) and selects nothing.
2. The same filter builds the `all_tests` pool used by import-graph expansion, so `test-*.mjs` files can never be selected there either.
3. Emission of a node command requires a selected `.mjs` path, so no `node --test` command is produced at all.

Verified while delivering SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C: editing three test files (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs`) produced a changed-scope command containing only `pytest ...` — no `node --test`. 46 of the 47 `tests/unit/*.mjs` files use the `test-` prefix, so the gap covers almost the whole node unit suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_is_test_file()` recognises `test-*.mjs` (and the equivalent `test-*.js`/`test-*.ts` naming) as test files.
- A unit test asserts that changing a `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` file selects `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` and causes a `node --test` command to be emitted by the changed-scope command builder (no pytest-only command).
- The selection never invents a path that does not exist (the existing LP-0MTZYRTNF0092JKW existence filter still applies).
- Existing changed-scope selection tests stay green; the full suite stays green.

## Constraints

- Do not widen selection to arbitrary `.mjs` helper files (e.g. `cli-helpers.mjs`); only the test-file naming conventions.
- Keep the single-source-of-truth rule: one filter function, no duplicated naming logic.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py`

# Refactor skill: never inject marker blocks above a shebang or encoding line

**Headline:** After the shebang fix (SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F) the refactor skill
still prepends its marker block above a PEP 263 encoding line and above a
Python module docstring, so annotated files implicitly change the file
encoding cookie position that the interpreter reads and trample the module
docstring convention. It also rewrites files without preserving line endings.
The remaining fix: compute an insertion offset from the file head (shebang,
then coding line, then optional module docstring) and splice the marker
block *below* all of them, writing with `newline=""`.

## Problem statement

`skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` places the REFACTOR marker block at the
top of the file and only steps past a leading shebang. Two Python-specific
file-head constructs are still displaced:

1. A **PEP 263 encoding declaration** (`# -*- coding: ... -*-`, or
   `# coding: ...`). PEP 263 requires the cookie on line 1, or line 2 when
   line 1 is a shebang. Prepending the marker pushes the cookie to line 3+,
   so Python no longer honours it — an encoding regression on files the skill
   touched. This gap was explicitly deferred by SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F (its
   "Open Questions" section records the cookie, out of scope there).
2. A **module docstring**. Prepending the marker above a leading module
   docstring splits the docstring from the module head; it also breaks the
   convention that the docstring is the first statement, and produces a
   noisier diff. AC1 therefore places the marker after the docstring too.

A third defect: the file is written with `open(..., "w")` and default line
handling, which can normalise line endings (CRLF → LF) — AC3 requires writing
with `newline=""` so line endings and trailing-newline state are preserved.

Leaving these unhandled means the skill keeps creating preventable lint
findings and file mutations on annotated scripts.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement
  pipeline's refactor step — they inherit preventable file-head mutations and
  encoding-changes on files the skill touched.
- **Producers triaging the refactor backlog** — self-inflicted findings
  consume triage and implementation capacity.
- **Developers** — annotated scripts must keep a valid encoding declaration
  (when present) and a clean module head.

User stories:

- As an agent running the refactor step, I want the marker block inserted
  *after* any shebang, encoding line, and module docstring, so annotated
  Python files keep their interpreter directive on line 1, their encoding
  cookie where the interpreter reads it, and their docstring as the first
  statement.
- As a maintainer, I want files the skill annotates to remain byte-stable
  apart from the marker (no line-ending normalisation), so diffs are minimal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `inject_refactor_comment()` inserts its block *after* any shebang
      (`#!…`) and any PEP 263 coding line, and after a Python module docstring
      when the file opens with one; on files with none of these the block
      still goes to the top as today.
- [ ] Markdown/HTML block-style markers (`<!-- … -->`) keep their current
      placement behaviour, except that a leading shebang or coding line in a
      non-Markdown file is never displaced.
- [ ] Line endings and trailing newline state are preserved (write with
      `newline=""`), so the fix does not normalise CRLF files.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` cover: a file
      starting with a shebang, a file with shebang + coding line, a file with
      shebang + docstring, a plain Python file with no shebang, and a Markdown
      file — each asserting shebang stays on line 1.
- [ ] A regression test asserts that running the repository's lint gate over a
      file annotated by the skill reports no `EXE005`/`EXE001`-style executable
      findings.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (the "REFACTOR Comments"
      section), and any relevant docs entries.

## Impact

Agents and producers no longer see self-inflicted encoding/executable-bit
findings or docstring trampling on files the refactor skill annotates; every
annotated script keeps its shebang, encoding declaration, and module docstring
exactly where the interpreter and tools expect them.

## Constraints

- Do **not** change marker syntax, the duplicate-suppression match on smell
  type, or `get_comment_style()` file-type mapping — placement only.
- Removal of stale markers on work-item close is **out of scope**; that is
  `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`.
- Keep the change confined to `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` and its
  tests (plus the SKILL.md/docs wording noted in the last AC).

## Existing state

Since SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F, `inject_refactor_comment()` steps past a leading
shebang via `_split_leading_shebang()` and splices the block immediately
below it (dropping the block's own leading newline). The remaining gaps:

```python
# skill/refactor/comment_injection.py
    shebang, body = _split_leading_shebang(original_content)
    if shebang:
        new_content = shebang + comment_block.lstrip("
") + body
    else:
        new_content = comment_block + original_content   # still displaces
                                                         # coding line / docstring

    with open(file_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:    # no newline=""
        f.write(new_content)
```

- A file opening with `# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-` (no shebang) gets the marker
  above the cookie — the cookie then sits at line 2+, which PEP 263 only
  allows when line 1 is a shebang.
- A file opening with a module docstring gets the marker above it.
- The write path does not preserve line endings (no `newline=""`).
- Field evidence: on 2026-10-30 the implement pipeline's refactor step
  annotated `src/rss_server.py` in the ContentCreator project, pushing
  `#!/usr/bin/env python3` from line 1 to line 13 and producing
  `EXE005 Shebang should be at the beginning of the file`. The finding was
  filed as `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0`, implemented as removing the skill's own
  marker, and pinned with `tests/test_rss_script_entrypoint.py`.

## Desired change

`inject_refactor_comment()` computes an insertion offset from the file head
(shebang, then coding line, then optional module docstring) and splices the
block there, leaving the file head byte-identical otherwise. Extend the
shebang-only helper into a general file-head skipper:

- Step past a leading `#!` line (existing behaviour, preserved).
- Step past a PEP 263 encoding declaration on line 1 (no shebang) or line 2
  (after a shebang) — Python-only concern; the marker belongs below the
  cookie, wherever it sits.
- Step past a leading Python module docstring (a triple-quoted string that
  opens the file body and terminates before the first statement). Heuristic:
  match only a leading `"""…"""`/`'''…'''` that closes before any statement;
  fall back to top-of-file placement when parsing is ambiguous
  (see Risks).
- Write the result with `newline=""` so CRLF and trailing-newline state are
  preserved.

Note for the implementer: with docstring placement the marker moves below
the docstring, so the current `TestShebangPreservation` case that asserts
marker-before-docstring (`content.index("REFACTOR") <
content.index('"""Docstring."""')`) must be updated to assert
marker-after-docstring per AC1. `has_existing_comment()` scans the whole
file, so markers below the docstring are still detected (idempotence
holds).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — generalise the file-head skip
  (shebang → coding line → docstring); write with `newline=""`
- `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — placement tests for the
  shebang / coding-line / docstring / Markdown cases; update the affected
  shebang+docstring assertion
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — state the placement rule in the "REFACTOR
  Comments" section
- `docs/refactor.md` — add the placement rule to the comment-injection
  documentation (if a suitable section exists)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a marker placed after the module docstring is still found by
  `has_existing_comment()`, which scans the whole file rather than the head.
- **Risk (low):** docstring detection is heuristic; an over-eager match could
  move the marker into the middle of code. Mitigation: match only a leading
  triple-quoted string that terminates before the first statement, and fall
  back to top-of-file placement when parsing is ambiguous.
- **Risk (low):** mis-detecting a leading `"…"`/`'…'` string literal as a
  docstring would displace the marker. Constrain detection to triple-quoted
  strings and, where practical, to files whose extension maps to the `.py`
  style.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a general "annotation lifecycle" refactor (placement,
  removal, sweep) is tempting. Record such work against
  `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`/`SA-0MVZA21600087VRD` instead of widening this item.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F` (completed) — fixed shebang displacement only; its
  deferred PEP 263 cookie question is this item's core scope. Partial overlap
  (shebang placement already shipped) — this item addresses the gaps.
- `SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD` (open) — refactor-skill file-size detection; adjacent
  refactor-skill concern, distinct from comment placement (mutually linked).
- `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` — remove stale `REFACTOR-` markers when their work
  item closes (marker lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `SA-0MVZA21600087VRD` — reap `REFACTOR-` marker blocks when the recorded
  smell is fixed (marker lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `SA-0MWFW1ZDT006VYM4` (blocked) — implement: unified parser and
  `remove_refactor_marker()` (marker lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `SA-0MWFW1YQ8007E2CZ` (open) — test: REFACTOR marker removal API (marker
  lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` — the ContentCreator item that this defect created
  (fixed by deleting the marker and pinning the entrypoint contract).
- `OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW` — the ContentCreator sweep of stale markers left in
  tests and scripts.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required: the work item description and the
  completed predecessor (SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F, whose scope notes explicitly
  deferred the encoding-cookie question) fully specify the gap, and the
  related-work search found no duplicate or overlapping open item. Recorded
  here for auditability.
  - Research: inspected `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` (shebang
    handled; coding line, docstring, and `newline=""` unhandled),
    `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` (shebang tests present;
    one assertion contradicts the new docstring AC and must be updated),
    `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` "REFACTOR Comments" section (placement rule
    absent), and ran `wl search` duplicate checks (no full duplicate; partial
    overlap with completed SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F only).

# Port the post-checkout / post-merge / post-rewrite hooks to the repo-root v2 wrappers

**Headline:** The three committed Worklog hooks are `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1`
wrappers that `exec` an absolute per-machine path,
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. When that path is absent (any
machine where `scripts/install_pi.sh` has not run), every checkout, merge and
`git worktree add` fails with `exec: … not found` (exit 127) and the post-pull
`wl sync` never runs — which broke `wl sync` in this repository on 2026-10-30
until `scripts/install_pi.sh` was re-run.

## Problem statement

`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` closed the "nothing creates the central script" half of
the problem by installing it from `install_pi.sh`. The remaining half is the
hard-coded absolute path itself: the hooks only work on a machine where the
installer ran, and a relocation or a fresh host silently disables the Worklog
sync. `ContentCreator` already migrated its hooks to `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2`
wrappers that resolve the delegate from the repository root
(`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) and fail open; this repository still ships the
v1 form.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** — `implement.py start/finish` and `wl sync` abort
  with exit 127 whenever git creates a worktree or checks out a branch on a
  machine without the central hook.
- **Developers on a fresh clone or a renamed checkout** — merges error on a
  hook they did not write and cannot see.
- **Producers** — Worklog data silently stops syncing when the hook errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge` and
      `.githooks/post-rewrite` carry the `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2` marker,
      resolve `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`,
      `cd` there, and `exec` it.
- [ ] All three wrappers are fail-open: no resolvable repository root, a missing
      delegate, or a missing `wl`/`worklog` exits 0 so a merge or checkout never
      fails because of the hook.
- [ ] `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` still short-circuits the sync (delegate
      behaviour unchanged).
- [ ] Tests prove the hooks work with `$HOME` unset or pointing at a sandbox and
      without any `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, from the
      repository root and from a subdirectory, for all three wrappers.
- [ ] A test scans `.githooks/` and fails if any file regains a hard-coded
      absolute checkout path (the `ContentCreator` equivalent lives in
      `tests/test_worklog_hooks.py`).
- [ ] `scripts/install_pi.sh` no longer warns that the wrappers do not delegate
      to the central path, and either stops installing the central script or
      documents it as legacy.
- [ ] `docs/dev/` hook documentation describes the v2 wrappers and the fail-open
      contract.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the `docs/dev/` hook pages.

## Constraints

- Keep `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` as the single implementation of the
  post-pull sync; the wrappers stay thin.
- Do not change the pre-push hook or its gates.
- Removal of the central-script install from `install_pi.sh` is optional; if it
  stays, it must not be required for the hooks to work.

## Existing state

```
$ cat .githooks/post-checkout
#!/bin/sh
# worklog:post-pull-hook:v1
# Wrapper that delegates to central Worklog post-pull script (committed hooks).
exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"
```

Observed failure (2026-10-30, `wl sync` in this repository):

```
✗ Sync failed: Command failed with exit code 127: git worktree add --detach '…/.worklog/tmp-worktree-yZC0Kd/wt' 'refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data'
Preparing worktree (detached HEAD a07575c13)
/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
```

Running `scripts/install_pi.sh` created
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` and the sync then succeeded — a
workaround, not a fix.

## Desired change

Replace the three v1 wrappers with the v2 wrapper (see
`ContentCreator/.githooks/post-merge` for the canonical text), extend
`tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` (or a new hook test module) with the
`$HOME`-independent cases, and update `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the docs to
match.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-checkout` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-merge` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-rewrite` — v2 wrapper
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` — hook behaviour without the central
  script; hard-coded-path scan
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — stop requiring the central script; drop the
  delegation warning
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — v2 wrapper contract (the post-pull hook page;
  there is no `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md`)

## Plan: changelog

- `2026-11-14` (plan skill, SA-0MVVFAM0P002PZYI): pre-check returned
  `skip` (effort Small, risk Low) so no child decomposition was created; the
  item is sized for direct implementation.
- `2026-11-14` (plan skill): corrected the `Key Files` doc reference from
  `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (does not exist) to `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`,
  which is the post-pull hook page that already documents the portable
  wrappers and fail-open contract and must be updated to the v2 shape.
- `2026-11-14` (plan skill): noted that `SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX` already made the
  committed wrappers portable (repo → local → `$HOME` resolution with the
  `v1` marker); the remaining work is the v2 repo-root-only shape (per
  `ContentCreator/.githooks/post-merge`), so the "existing state" described
  above is historical context, not the current checkout.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` works when executed from the
  repository root; that is how `post-merge` already invokes it.
- **Risk (low):** a `post-checkout` run inside `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (the
  Worklog data branch) would sync from that temporary checkout. Mitigation: the
  delegate is already fail-open and warns on failure; verify it does not
  recurse when the temporary worktree has no `.worklog`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** consolidating the hooks with the ContentCreator copy
  into one shared installer is tempting. Record that separately; this item only
  ports the v2 wrapper shape.

## Related work

- `SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` — installs the central post-pull script (the other half
  of the same failure mode).
- `SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX` — fail-open portability warning added to
  `install_pi.sh`.
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` (ContentCreator) — the item whose `wl sync` surfaced
  this failure.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP** – Chore: install central wl post-pull hook (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing (completed)
- **SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX** – Commit hooks exec a missing absolute path (/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) → git worktree add and wl sync fail (completed)
- **SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6** – SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing central script (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: abort, absent, absolute, acceptance, add (+205 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: abort, absent, absolute, acceptance, add (+203 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: abort, absent, absolute, acceptance, add (+194 more)
