# Add near-duplicate test detection to find redundant test coverage

## Goal

As a maintainer of a large test suite, I want the test-value tooling to report
near-duplicate test blocks and files, so additive accumulation can be measured
and redundant coverage pruned with evidence instead of suspicion.

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measured large net test growth (+137,022 lines, +384
files on the reference project) against a **low** rewrite ratio (14.0%
modified-only), so the suite grows by *additive accumulation*, not churn. The
only existing redundancy check — `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`'s
"duplicate coverage" veto — matches test *names* containing `again|also covers|
duplicate|already covered` inside a single file. It cannot see a copy-pasted
test with renamed identifiers, nor the same behaviour re-tested through a
different import path, so redundancy accumulates with nothing forcing a
re-examination.

## Users

- **Producer / engineering manager** — wants the *size* of the redundancy, not
  just total growth, to decide whether pruning is worth runtime.
- **Implementer of the test-value refactor epic** (`SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`) —
  needs block-level, line-range evidence for the Classify and Prove steps; the
  epic's AC3 forbids deleting a test on suspicion alone.
- **Agent working a prune pass** — needs a deterministic, read-only command
  whose JSON can be joined with churn and usefulness data.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I want a ranked list of duplicate test clusters with redundant
  line counts so I can see how much of the growth is redundancy.
- As the refactor implementer, I want each cluster to name the file and line
  range of every member so a prune candidate can be proven, not guessed.
- As an agent, I want `expected-repetition` (parametrised/table-driven cases)
  excluded by the tool so I do not file bogus prune items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — **Detection is structural, not textual.** Near-duplicate test blocks are detected within and across files using normalised representation: Python test blocks via `ast` (docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches), JavaScript/TypeScript/other test files via comment-stripped token normalisation with brace-matched block boundaries. Raw text equality is never the similarity measure.
- [ ] AC2 — **Clusters are reported with location and score.** Each cluster lists every member's file path, start–end line range, block size (lines and tokens), member-to-member and cluster similarity score, and a redundancy measure (member lines minus the largest member's lines) used to order the report. Both `test_duplicates.json` (versioned schema: thresholds, method, limitations, clusters) and `test_duplicate_report.md` (human, same content, ordered by redundancy) are written to `--output-dir`.
- [ ] AC3 — **Conservatism and legitimate repetition.** Parametrised/table-driven repetition is classified `expected-repetition`, not redundancy: `pytest.mark.parametrize`, `unittest.subTest`, `test.each`/`it.each`, and blocks whose sweep is a data loop over case literals are detected and excluded. Similarity bands are explicit (`duplicate` ≥ threshold, default 0.85; `near-duplicate` between the lower band, default 0.65, and the threshold), every cluster carries a `report-only` verdict, and the tool never edits, deletes or renames anything.
- [ ] AC4 — **Performance is bounded and documented.** Defaults skip trivial blocks (`--min-lines`, default 10) and bound the candidate set; comparison uses an inverted shingle index plus optional MinHash banding rather than all-pairs O(n²). Scope options `--changed-only <base-ref>` (git diff), `--max-files N`, `--min-lines N`, `--threshold` and `--min-shared-tokens` are documented with the complexity they imply, and a measured runtime figure for a ~500-test-file suite is recorded in the docs and in the report preamble.
- [ ] AC5 — **Behaviour is pinned by tests.** Unit tests cover: normalisation invariance (a copy with renamed identifiers still scores ≥ threshold), distinct behaviour staying below the band, `expected-repetition` exclusion for parametrised and table-driven cases, threshold boundary behaviour, cluster ordering and redundant-line arithmetic, JSON and Markdown schema/content, an empty or single-block suite, a non-Python file set, and one end-to-end run over a fixture suite. Every test asserts one documented behaviour and no test re-implements the similarity algorithm under test.
- [ ] AC6 — **Documentation is updated.** `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` gains a "Near-duplicate detection" section wired into the existing pruning workflow (step 2 "inspect candidates" gains the command as the evidence source for the duplicate-coverage bullet); `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` records the method, thresholds, complexity/runtime bound, worked example and limitations; the `README.md` skill line mentions it; and the docs state that this analyser supersedes `evaluate_usefulness.py`'s name-marker heuristic for near-duplicates. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] AC7 — **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A maintainer can see — ranked by redundant line count — exactly which test
blocks duplicate each other and prune them on recorded evidence, instead of
inferring redundancy from a raw growth number.

## Constraints

- **Read-only.** No automatic deletion, editing or renaming of test files; no
  writes outside `--output-dir`.
- **Conservative thresholds.** A false "duplicate" verdict is worse than a
  miss: uncertainty reports, never removes.
- **No hardcoded project paths.** Test/source classification and language
  handling follow the configurable, language-neutral approach already used by
  `ChurnConfig`; extend it rather than forking it.
- **Python standard library only.** The repository has zero third-party
  dependencies (`package.json` `dependencies: {}`, no `requirements.txt`); no
  tree-sitter/esprima/acorn dependency may be added.
- **No network, no per-block subprocess.** The analyser must not shell out to
  `node`, `pytest` or a language server; all parsing is in-process.
- **Deterministic output.** Same tree and flags ⇒ byte-identical JSON, so
  results are comparable over time (the churn analyser's existing property).

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` (1,586 lines) — history-based
  churn: `ChurnConfig`, `is_test_file`, `classify_area`, `build_report`,
  `write_outputs`, CLI (`--project-root --branch --since --max-commits
  --output-dir --config --format --stdout --quiet`). It measures *how test code
  changes over time*; it contains no similarity analysis and never reads test
  bodies.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` (279 lines) — per-file verdicts.
  `_detect_duplicate` is a name-marker regex plus "imports production code";
  `VERDICT_REPORT` is always used for duplicate-only findings.
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — anti-pattern 4 "duplicates of
  existing core coverage" (same behaviour via a different import path) is prose
  with no automated check; the churn skill's pruning workflow names it but
  offers only a manual grep.
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::jaccard_similarity` — word-token Jaccard over
  *text* strings; precedent for the metric, unusable for code ASTs (no
  normalisation, no block boundaries).
- `skill/test-churn/tests/` — `conftest.py` loads the analyser by path
  (`test_churn_analysis_under_test`) so it is not collected as a test module;
  `.pi/test-config.json` has no `test-churn` group, so these tests currently run
  only under `full`.

## Desired change

A new read-only analyser `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py`
with a CLI shaped like its churn sibling:

1. **Collect** test files using the existing classification (`is_test_file` +
   `ChurnConfig`), honouring `--changed-only <base-ref>` / `--max-files`.
2. **Extract blocks** with file + line range: Python via `ast` (top-level
   functions/classes/methods plus `with`-wrapped test bodies), JS/TS and other
   languages via comment-stripped tokenisation with brace/paren matching. Blocks
   smaller than `--min-lines` are skipped.
3. **Normalise** (docstrings and comments dropped, identifiers mapped to
   positional placeholders per scope, literals canonicalised by type, whitespace
   collapsed) so renamed copies remain identical while different behaviour does
   not.
4. **Fingerprint and compare**: token k-gram shingles (k default 5) → Jaccard
   similarity; candidates from an inverted shingle index (optionally MinHash
   banding) instead of all pairs; file-level rollup reports the strongest block
   pair per file pair.
5. **Classify** each pair as `duplicate`, `near-duplicate` or
   `expected-repetition` (parametrisation/data-loop detection), then cluster
   transitively and order clusters by redundant lines.
6. **Write** `test_duplicate_report.md` + `test_duplicates.json` with method,
   thresholds, limitations and measured runtime in the preamble; print a
   one-line summary to stderr.

The script is wired into the churn skill's pruning workflow and reference docs;
`evaluate_usefulness.py` keeps its heuristic unchanged (it answers a different,
per-file question) but its duplicate-coverage reason cross-references the new
tool.

## Key Files

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py` — **new** analyser: block extraction, normalisation, shingling/Jaccard, clustering, JSON + Markdown writers, CLI.
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` — reuse `ChurnConfig`/`is_test_file`/`classify_area`; factor any shared helpers rather than duplicating them (no behaviour change to existing metrics).
- `skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py` — **new** unit + end-to-end suite for the analyser.
- `skill/test-churn/tests/conftest.py` — add a path-loaded fixture for the new module (same pattern as `churn`).
- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` — new "Near-duplicate detection" section; pruning-workflow step 2 gains the command.
- `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` — method, thresholds, complexity/runtime bound, worked example, limitations.
- `README.md` — extend the test-churn bullet to name near-duplicate detection.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` — docstring/reason cross-reference to the new tool (no behaviour change).
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — anti-pattern 4 gains the automated-evidence pointer.
- `.pi/test-config.json` — optional: add a `test-churn` group (`skill/test-churn/**`) so changed-scope runs execute these tests instead of falling through to `full`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **False-positive duplicates** (shared boilerplate, fixture setup, mechanical
  parameter sweeps) are the dominant risk and the reason for report-only
  verdicts: mitigation is the `expected-repetition` classifier, a conservative
  default threshold of 0.85 with a separate `near-duplicate` band, `--min-lines`
  skipping trivial blocks, and a documented limitations section.
- **Parser fragility outside Python** — brace matching on JS/TS is approximate;
  mitigation is conservative fallback (a block that cannot be delimited is
  reported as "unparsed" in the JSON summary rather than silently compared as a
  whole file), plus a non-Python fixture in the tests.
- **Performance on large suites** — shingle construction is linear in tokens,
  but candidate pairing can still blow up; mitigation is the inverted index,
  `--max-files`/`--changed-only` scope options and a measured runtime figure
  recorded in the docs.
- **Scope creep** — "also fix the duplicated tests" is explicitly out of scope:
  remediation belongs to the epic's prune/rework children. Any duplication the
  tool finds in this repository is reported as evidence in a comment or a
  follow-on item, not fixed here.
- **Assumption A1** — the detector belongs beside the churn analyser in
  `skill/test-churn/` rather than inside `evaluate_usefulness.py`, because it is
  suite-wide measurement, not a per-file verdict, and the churn skill is where
  the pruning workflow lives.
- **Assumption A2** — no new third-party parser dependency (stdlib only), so
  JS/TS detection is token-based rather than AST-based; Python gets exact AST
  normalisation.
- **Assumption A3** — the item stays `discovered-from:SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`
  rather than being re-parented under `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`; the epic's
  Classify/Prove children consume its output, and re-parenting a
  `plan_complete` epic would change that epic's scope.
- **Assumption A4** — a `test-churn` test group does not exist in
  `.pi/test-config.json` today; adding one is a small, separable improvement
  that keeps these tests out of the `full`-only path (optional within this
  item).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic; additive accumulation is its
  stated failure mode and this analyser feeds its Classify and Prove steps.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing; a direct fault-detection signal that
  complements this cheap redundancy signal (discovery source for this item).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over
  `toHaveBeenCalledWith`; overlapping "rework" direction, different evidence.
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — integrate test-churn metrics into the refactor skill:
  a natural consumer of this output.
- Code: `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`,
  `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`,
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (anti-pattern 4),
  `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Duplicate-work check performed with `wl search` over "duplicate test", "clone
detection", "test redundancy" and "near-duplicate … coverage" — no completed or
open item overlaps these acceptance criteria (the nearest hits are intake
duplicate-work detection `SA-0MTWMCJ37000485M` and the refactor skill's
`consolidate_duplicates.py`, both different problems: work-item duplication and
duplicated *work items*, not duplicated test blocks).

No interactive interview round was held: the seed description already carried a
problem statement, six acceptance criteria, constraints and related work, so the
intake was driven by repository research instead of questions. The four open
design decisions were resolved as documented assumptions for review:

- Q: "Where should the near-duplicate detector live — extend
  `evaluate_usefulness.py`, or a new script beside the churn analyser?" —
  **Answer (agent assumption A1, pending producer confirmation):** new script

# Intake Brief: Repeat producer actions in red on the final report conclusion

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report`) lists blocking producer
actions in `## Producer Actions`, but the `## Conclusion` — the last thing the
operator reads — does not repeat them. When a session ends with something the
producer must do (answer a question, make a decision, grant an approval), the
operator can miss it in the body of a long report. Repeating any genuine
producer action in the Conclusion in red makes the blocking call-to-action
impossible to overlook.

## Users

- **Producer/operator** reading end-of-session reports in the pi TUI: wants the
  blocking action to stand out at the end of the report, not be buried mid-page.
- **Agent (intake/plan/implement/audit/…) authoring the report**: keeps passing
  blocking actions via `--producer-actions`; the renderer handles the red
  repetition deterministically (no per-skill change).

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when a skill session needs a decision from me, I want that
  decision repeated in red in the conclusion so I cannot miss it."
- "As a producer, when nothing is required of me, I do not want a red warning in
  the conclusion."
- "As an agent, I want the renderer to do this automatically so every skill
  behaves the same way."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the normalised producer actions are a genuine, non-`None needed`
   action, `render_report()` appends the action text **verbatim** to the
   `## Conclusion` section, wrapped in ANSI SGR red (`\x1b[31m…\x1b[0m`) with a
   `⚠️ Producer action required:` lead-in. Verified by unit test asserting the
   escape sequences and the exact action text inside `## Conclusion`.
2. When no producer actions are supplied, or the supplied text is routine
   workflow progression that normalises to `None needed`, the Conclusion
   contains no ANSI escape sequences and no repeated action text. Verified by
   unit tests (absent actions; `Proceed to /skill:plan`; `Review the brief, then
   run /skill:plan`).
3. Colour can be disabled with a new `--no-colour` CLI flag **or** the standard
   `NO_COLOR` environment variable (non-empty). In that mode the Conclusion
   still repeats the action in plain text with the `⚠️` marker and contains no
   ANSI escape sequences. Verified by unit tests for both opt-outs.
4. Multi-line / multi-action producer text is repeated verbatim (line breaks
   preserved) and the rest of the report is unchanged: section order,
   `## Producer Actions` → `## Notes` → `## Conclusion`, the existing
   completed/incomplete conclusion sentences, and the `</end_session>`
   terminator. Verified by regression tests.
5. `skill/report/SKILL.md` documents the conditional red repetition in the
   canonical template, the layout rules, and the colour opt-out
   (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`) alongside the existing icon opt-out. Verified
   by document review.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Implement in the shared renderer only (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  plus a small shared colour helper — do not fork report logic into the ~17
  calling skills.
- Repeat **after** routine-next-step normalisation (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW): a
  routine next step must never produce red text.
- Do not use TTY detection to decide colour: the CLI's stdout is captured/piped
  by agents before being pasted into the final response, so TTY detection would
  disable the feature exactly where it is needed. Opt-out must be explicit
  (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`).
- Colour is decorative: the `⚠️` marker and the plain action text must carry the
  meaning when colour is unavailable, so the report stays readable in
  non-ANSI consumers (GitHub, plain-text logs).
- No new runtime dependency; pure-Python, offline-testable.
- Do not change `## Producer Actions` semantics, the pane-status derivation, or
  the existing conclusion wording.

## Existing state

- `render_report()` renders `## Producer Actions` from the normalised
  `producer_actions` string (`None needed` when absent), then `## Notes`, then
  `## Conclusion`.
- The Conclusion currently emits one of two fixed sentences based on AC
  verdicts (`_derive_session_status`): completed → "This completes … Ready for
  `<next_action>`."; incomplete → "… is incomplete. Requires attention
  (`<next_action>`)." Nothing else is appended.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` already provides `icons_enabled(no_icons, env)`
  honouring `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` — the convention to mirror for
  colour, but colour must be a separate switch (`WL_NO_ICONS` must not disable
  colour).
- No ANSI/colour handling exists anywhere in the report renderer today (the
  only ANSI in the repo is in `tests/integration/test-worktree-workflow.sh`).

## Desired change

- Add `colour_enabled(no_colour=False, env=None)` (and `RED`/`RESET` constants)
  to `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`: enabled by default; disabled by
  `--no-colour` or a non-empty `NO_COLOR`.
- In `render_report()`, after the existing conclusion sentence(s), when the
  normalised producer actions are not `None needed`, append a blank line and a
  red line: `⚠️ Producer action required: <verbatim action text>`. Apply
  `RED … RESET` only when colour is enabled.
- Thread an optional `no_colour: bool = False` parameter through
  `render_report()`, `render_report_from_workitem()`, `render_from_wl()` and the
  CLI, adding the `--no-colour` flag.
- Update `skill/report/SKILL.md` (template, layout rules, example, colour
  opt-out) and the `README.md` report-helper bullet to mention the red
  repetition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — conditional red repetition in the
  Conclusion; `no_colour` plumbing and `--no-colour` flag.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` helper + `RED`/`RESET`
  constants mirroring `icons_enabled()`.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — new tests: red repetition,
  no-repetition for absent/routine actions, `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR` fallback,
  multi-line preservation, structure regression.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` unit tests.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — template/layout/example + colour opt-out docs.
- `README.md` — report-helper bullet: note the red repetition of blocking
  producer actions in the Conclusion.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** — "Don't include producer actions that are next steps"
  (completed): established normalisation to `None needed`; the red repetition
  must run after it.
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — "Misleading completion message on LLM summaries"
  (completed): made the Conclusion reflect session status; this item extends the
  same section.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — "Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion" (completed): established the ✅/⚠️/🚫 status colour semantics this
  feature reuses for a red call-to-action.
- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill" (completed): origin of the canonical report contract.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "red font" means ANSI SGR red in terminal output.** The report
  is rendered to stdout and pasted into the pi TUI; ANSI is the only mechanism
  that reliably colours that path. If the producer expects Markdown/HTML
  colouring, the brief should be revised before implementation (documented in
  the Appendix).
- **Assumption — red repeats blocking actions only.** Because routine workflow
  progression is normalised to `None needed` first, it can never trigger red;
  this avoids the false "producer is blocking" signal fixed by
  SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW.
- **Assumption — no TTY detection.** Explicit opt-out only, because agent-captured
  stdout is not a TTY.
- **Risk — ANSI leakage into non-terminal consumers** (GitHub, PRs, plain logs).
  Mitigation: `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR`, plus the `⚠️` marker and plain text so the
  meaning survives even if escapes are stripped or shown literally.
- **Risk — colour-blindness / theme contrast.** Mitigation: the `⚠️` marker and
  the words "Producer action required" carry the signal; colour is decorative.
- **Risk — multi-line producer text.** Mitigation: wrap the whole block once and
  test line-break preservation rather than prefixing each line.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent ideas (colouring the `## Producer Actions` section,
  colourising AC verdicts, HTML-export colour) are out of scope — record as
  separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'red font' mean for a Markdown report rendered by the LLM/TUI —
  ANSI escape codes, HTML `<span style=\"color:red\">`, or plain emphasis?"
  — **Answer (repo research + design analysis):** ANSI SGR red. The report is
  printed to stdout and pasted into the terminal-rendered TUI; raw ANSI passes
  through and colours the terminal, whereas inline HTML styles are not honoured
  by the Markdown→terminal path and GitHub strips `style` attributes. Recorded
  as an assumption; the producer can request an HTML/bold variant at review.
  No interactive round was required for the rest of the brief.
- Q: "Should routine next-step actions (e.g. 'Proceed to /skill:plan') also be
  repeated in red?" — **Answer (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW contract):** No. Routine
  workflow progression is normalised to `None needed` and must never be shown as
  a blocking red action; only genuine, current-stage actions are repeated.
- Q: "Should colour be auto-detected (TTY) or explicitly opt-out?" — **Answer
  (design analysis):** Explicit opt-out only. Agent-captured stdout is not a
  TTY, so TTY detection would silently disable the feature on the exact path
  that needs it. `--no-colour` and `NO_COLOR` are the opt-outs.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVQ1QM9L0083KAW** – Producer Actions contract: docs and skill templates (completed)
- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** – Don't include producer actions that are next steps (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: action, actions, conclusion, final, llm, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there

## Goal

`_git_commit_evidence` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` resolves a
stranded child's pushed-commit evidence with
`git log <ref> --grep <child_id> -n 1`. `--grep` matches the **whole commit
message including the body**, so a commit that merely *mentions* a work-item id
counts as that item's work.

Observed 2026-11-01 during the epic drive for SA-0MVX1M6HH004YPX2: driven child
SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 timed out after 3600 s with its own commit (`9119e4117`)
still unpushed in its worktree, and `drive` reported it as *stranded* with
evidence `0fb0e4305` — the **sibling** child's (SA-0MVX31GLC002IPR8) commit,
whose body names SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 as the future home of the detection
module. The verdict told the operator to `--finalise-stranded` a child whose
work had never been pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Commit evidence matches only commits whose **subject** references the
   work-item id, never a body-only mention.
2. A regression test pins the false-positive: a commit whose body mentions
   another item's id is not evidence for that item.
3. A driven child whose commit is still only in its own worktree is reported
   as non-terminal-with-work, not as stranded on the parent branch.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_git_commit_evidence`
- `skill/implement/tests/` — regression test

# Intake brief — re-filed from OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ (ContentCreator worklog)

**Headline:** Add a consumption mechanism to the refactor skill so that `# <!-- REFACTOR-<id> ... -->` marker blocks are automatically detected as stale and flagged (or removed) when their recorded smell is fixed.

## Problem statement

The refactor skill injects `# <!-- REFACTOR-<work-item-id> ... -->` blocks into source files to record code smells. The expectation is that whoever fixes the smell also deletes the block. Nothing checks that this happened. Three stale blocks were found in a single sweep, and one live marker remains — proving the gap is ongoing, not a one-off.

## Users

- **Maintainer opening a file.** A stale marker asserts a live smell; disproving it requires a worklog lookup and wastes time.
- **The refactor skill itself (next run).** A stale block reads as a live smell and invites a duplicate work item.
- **The operator running periodic sweeps.** Currently they must manually delete each stale block (OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW).

**User story:** "As a developer running the refactor skill or reading a file, I want stale REFACTOR markers to be flagged or removed automatically, so that the tree only contains markers for unfinished work."

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- The refactor skill writes markers via `comment_injection.py`; no corresponding consumption code exists.
- Markers contain: `REFACTOR-<id>`, `smell: <type>`, `severity: <level>`, `description: <text>`, and optionally `# status: resolved — <reason>`.
- OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW removed three stale blocks by hand (completed). The consumption gap was recorded as this item (discovered-from:OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW).
- One live marker remains in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py:2` (OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L, ruff C408) — this is correct and should stay until the smell is fixed.
- The `# status: resolved` line exists in at least one marker (`scripts/tidy_residual_links.py`) but is not parsed by any tool.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The refactor skill exposes a reusable function `reap_stale_markers()` (or similar) that scans files for `# <!-- REFACTOR-... -->` blocks and returns a list of stale markers — each entry identifying the file path, line range, work item ID, and the reason the marker is stale (work item terminal / `# status: resolved` present / work item missing).
2. A new CLI entry point `python3 -m skill.refactor.scripts.reap_stale_markers` invokes the function, prints a summary of stale markers found, and exits non-zero if any are discovered — suitable for pre-commit or CI.
3. When invoked with `--dry-run` (default), the tool reports stale markers without modifying files; when invoked with `--remove`, it deletes the marker blocks in-place and preserves all other file content exactly.
4. The function correctly classifies a marker as stale when: (a) the referenced work item's status is `completed` or `deleted` (soft-deleted), or (b) the marker block itself contains `# status: resolved`, or (c) the referenced work item cannot be found (missing or inaccessible) — reason `work-item-missing`. It must NOT flag a marker as stale if the smell is still unfixed (work item is `open` and no resolved line).
5. `python3 -m ruff check` stays clean over all affected files; no `noqa` or config suppression is added.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`./scripts/run_tests.sh`).

## Constraints

- Keep it out of `comment_injection.py` — that mechanism is correct; the gap is consumption.
- The tool must work with the Worklog CLI (`wl show --json`) to check item status; do not add a direct database dependency.
- Do not modify marker copies inside `.worklog/worktrees/*` — only process files in the source tree.
- The `# status: resolved` line format is `# status: resolved — <reason>`; parse this conservatively (presence of `status: resolved` is sufficient).
- If a marker references a work item that cannot be found (item does not exist or is inaccessible), treat it as stale with reason `work-item-missing`.

## Desired change

Add a new module `refactor/reap_markers.py` (or `refactor/consumption.py`) with the detection logic, a CLI entry point, and tests. The refactor skill's main scan should optionally invoke this as a pre-flight or post-flight check.

## Key Files

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — reference only; own the marker format, do not modify
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — reference only; understand `REFACTOR_PATTERN` matching
- `skill/refactor/reap_markers.py` — new module: detection logic + public API (`reap_stale_markers()`)
- `skill/refactor/scripts/reap_stale_markers.py` — new CLI entry point
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — document the reaper and its place in the scan lifecycle
- `tests/test_refactor/test_reap_markers.py` — new test file (mirrors `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py`)

## Related work

- `OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW` — Remove stale REFACTOR- marker blocks left in tests and scripts (completed) — manual sweep of three blocks
- `OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L` — Live marker in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py` (ruff C408) — should remain until fixed
- `OSL-0MVM96NMG002ZAMZ` — Recover orphaned refactor-batch edits (completed) — same marker mechanism, different problem
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` — Marker-above-shebang near miss (completed) — edge case for comment placement

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the Worklog CLI (`wl show`) is available and reliable for checking item status during the refactor skill's run. **Mitigation:** handle CLI errors gracefully (treat unreachable items as potentially stale with a warning).
- **Risk — false positive:** a marker could reference a completed item that is still relevant as historical context. **Mitigation:** default to `--dry-run` mode; require explicit `--remove` to delete.
- **Risk — scope creep:** turning this into a full repo-wide cleanup sweep. **Mitigation:** scope is the detection/reporting mechanism only; bulk removal is a separate concern.
- **Assumption:** `# status: resolved` is the canonical in-marker resolution signal. **Mitigation:** documented in the new module's docstring; the operator can update if the convention changes.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

No interview round was run: the problem, scope, constraints, and related work were answerable by repo and worklog search.

- **Q (resolved by search):** What markers currently exist in the repo? — **Answer:** one live marker in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py:2` (OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L, ruff C408, smell still unfixed) and three stale markers that were deleted by OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW. Source: grep, this session.
- **Q (resolved by search):** Is `# status: resolved` a real convention or just an ad-hoc line? — **Answer:** it appears on at least one marker (`scripts/tidy_residual_links.py`) and was noted in the OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW implementation report as evidence the smell was fixed. It is a convention worth formalising in the reap module. Source: `wl show OSL-0MVM4UWDI001GZNY`, this session.
- **Q (resolved by search):** Can the refactor skill invoke `wl`? — **Answer:** yes — the refactor skill's scripts already use the Worklog CLI (e.g., `wl list --tags Refactor`). Source: inspection of `comment_injection.py`, `workitem_creation.py`, this session.
- **Duplicate check:** `wl search "REFACTOR marker reap consumption stale"` returned only OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ itself and OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW (the manual sweep). No item covers automated consumption.

## Appendix: plan-session questions (plan skill)

Planning stopped at the interview step: the item cannot be decomposed into
implementation tasks until repository ownership is settled.

- **OPEN QUESTION (blocking; directed to the producer):** Which repository
  should the reap implementation land in? The item's ACs and Key Files target
  the shared/global refactor skill (AC1 "The refactor skill exposes a reusable
  function", Key Files `.pi/agent/skills/refactor/...`, AC2
  `python3 -m refactor.reap`), but that skill is developed in the **SorraAgents**
  repository (`skill/refactor/`, installed as the symlink
  `~/.pi/agent/skills -> ~/projects/SorraAgents/skill`) and every refactor-skill
  change is tracked there under SA- IDs (e.g. SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F,
  SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD). This item is filed in the **ContentCreator** worklog
  (OSL-). **Why it matters:** it decides which repo the code, tests and commits
  go into, and the implement skill's worktree isolation normally forbids
  editing outside the ContentCreator worktree.
  - Options: **(a)** re-file as an SA- item in the SorraAgents worklog and
    redirect/close this OSL item — *recommended*, matches every other
    refactor-skill change; **(b)** keep the OSL item and author cross-repo
    changes into SorraAgents from it — needs explicit authorisation;
    **(c)** rescope this OSL item to a ContentCreator-local reap tool (e.g.
    `scripts/reap_stale_markers.py` over ContentCreator's own tree) and relax
    AC1's skill wording.
  - Evidence gathered: `git ls-files | grep refactor` in ContentCreator returns
    0 paths; `.pi/agent/` does not exist in ContentCreator;
    `.pi/skills_extensions/` supports only `SKILL_PREFIX.md` / `SKILL_POSTFIX.md`
    / `extension.json` (prose and data, not Python modules).
  - **Preferred option: (a).**
  - **ANSWER (producer, this session): (a)** — re-file as an SA- item in the
    SorraAgents worklog and redirect this OSL item. FINAL. That re-filing is
    this work item; `OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ` was deleted after it was created.
- **Q (resolved by inspection, no operator input needed):** Where are the live
  REFACTOR markers today? — **Answer:** two. `tests/test_rss_freshness.py:1`
  (OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L, `complexity`, C408, item `open` — correctly *not*
  stale) and `tests/test_rss_regenerate.py:1` (OSL-0MVYHBV60007WKHK,
  `ruff_specific`, RUF059, item `open` — also not stale). Source: grep over
  the ContentCreator tree, this session. Note the second marker's work item
  records a *worktree* path (`<main>/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>`),
  which is relevant to the "do not modify marker copies inside
  `.worklog/worktrees/*`" constraint.
- **Q (resolved by inspection):** Does the marker format match what

## Problem statement

During `implement.py finish`, the refactor step detects pre-existing code smells and attempts to file a worklog work item for each. When work item creation is skipped (a guard hit: ephemeral worktree, file not found, duplicate REFACTOR comment, existing worklog item, audit twin) or fails (`wl create` error), `remediate_pre_existing()` silently drops the finding — it increments `comment_errors` and logs only a generic `"No work item ID for smell … skipping comment"` warning. Neither the guard that fired nor the failure reason reaches the finish report, so the framework's own lint debt accumulates invisibly: the observed run showed `pre_existing: 5`, `work_items_created: 0`, `comment_errors: 5` with no explanation of *why* every smell was dropped.

## Users

- **Producers** reviewing a finish report who need to know whether pre-existing lint debt is tracked or was silently dropped.
- **Agents** running `implement.py finish` that rely on the report to prove a clean gate rather than an unexamined one.

Example user story: *As a producer reviewing a finish report, I want every detected pre-existing smell to show either the work item that tracks it or the specific reason it was skipped, so I can trust that framework lint debt is not accumulating invisibly.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Every skipped pre-existing smell records its skip reason.** When `create_smell_work_item()` returns `None`, the refactor step records which guard fired (ephemeral `.worklog/worktrees` target, missing source file, existing REFACTOR comment, existing worklog item, audit-family twin, or `wl create` failure) for that specific smell.
2. **The finish report carries a per-smell remediation breakdown.** The refactor report's `remediation` section includes, for every pre-existing smell, its identity (smell type, code, repository-relative file) and either the created work-item ID (plus REFACTOR comment outcome) or the recorded skip reason — so `comment_errors: 5` is never the only signal.
3. **Findings are never silently lost.** For every detected pre-existing smell the report shows exactly one outcome — tracked (work item + comment) or explicitly explained-skipped — and the counts reconcile (`pre_existing == tracked + explained_skipped`). No smell is dropped without a recorded reason in the report.
4. **The finish gate surfaces the breakdown.** `implement.py finish` output (via `run_refactor()` → report) includes the per-smell remediation outcome so a producer sees the reason without reading raw refactor subprocess logs.
5. **Re-running `implement.py finish` on the same tree produces identical remediation outcomes** (idempotent — no duplicate work items, no duplicate report entries).
6. **Automated tests cover each skip reason** — a test per guard/failure path (ephemeral worktree, missing file, duplicate REFACTOR comment, existing worklog item, audit twin, `wl create` failure) asserting the reason reaches the report, plus a reconciliation test (`pre_existing == tracked + explained_skipped`).
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`).
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

Producers and agents can see exactly why each pre-existing smell finding was not tracked, so framework lint debt can no longer accumulate invisibly.

## Constraints

- Changes are confined to the refactor skill (`skill/refactor/`) and the reporting surface in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`run_refactor()` / finish report assembly).
- Must not change smell *detection* logic or work-item *creation* decision logic — only make existing decisions observable in the report.
- Must not add new external dependencies; reuse existing logging/report structures.
- Must preserve existing dedupe behaviour (same-identity grouping, existing-item reuse, audit-twin suppression) — those remain correct guards; only their outcome must become visible.

## Existing state

`remediate_pre_existing()` in `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` calls `create_smell_work_items_mapped()` then iterates smells to inject REFACTOR comments. `create_smell_work_item()` in `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` returns `None` from several guards, each logging only a `LOG.warning`/`LOG.info` line. When the mapped ID is `None`, `remediate_pre_existing()` increments `comment_errors` and logs a single generic warning. `run_refactor()` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` captures the refactor subprocess stdout as the report, so the finish report shows only `{"comment_errors": N}` with no per-smell breakdown.

## Desired change

Make the skip/track decision per smell observable in the refactor report:
- Introduce a structured per-smell outcome record (identity + `created` with item ID + comment status, or `skipped` with a reason enum) produced by the remediation pass and returned in the report's `remediation` section.
- Have `remediate_pre_existing()` collect these outcomes instead of only counting `comment_errors`, while keeping the existing guards unchanged.
- Ensure `run_refactor()` propagates the enriched remediation data into the finish report so `implement.py finish` shows the reasons.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — `remediate_pre_existing()` must record structured per-smell outcomes (created vs skipped + reason) instead of only incrementing `comment_errors`.
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — `create_smell_work_item()` guards must surface *which* guard fired (return-with-reason or a parallel outcome map), without changing the guards' decisions.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `run_refactor()` must propagate the enriched remediation breakdown into the finish report.
- `tests/test_refactor/` and `skill/implement/tests/` — new/updated tests covering each skip reason and the report breakdown.

## Related work

- **SA-0MW7Z1AU1006UT9C** (completed): Refactor dedupe — substring matching caused the same smell to be filed repeatedly.
- **SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG**: Same-identity grouping so each identity maps to a single work item (identity→item mapping used by comment injection).
- **SA-0MWE1EAR30045VHO**: Audit-family twin suppression (`ruff <RULE> in <path> — candidate false positive` chores).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MRCQ5K50007G3BB** – Add ready-to-close audit gate to ship skill release process (completed)
- **SA-0MQA71IRS002KU2O** – Code Comment Injection Module (completed)
- **SA-0MWFW1ZDT006VYM4** – Implement: unified parser and remove_refactor_marker() (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, accumulate, analyzed, auto, ble001 (+80 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mvze164p0048306, acceptance, accumulate, auto, ble001 (+77 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvze164p0048306, acceptance, auto, blind, blocking (+72 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the seed context (source log excerpt, the reported `remediation` JSON, and the identified call chain `remediate_pre_existing()` → `create_smell_work_items_mapped()` → `create_smell_work_item()`) already defined the problem and desired outcome. Requirements were derived from repository inspection.

- Q: "Does a pre-existing smell already create a work item on the happy path?" — Answer (research, agent): Yes — `create_smell_work_item()` creates an item and `remediate_pre_existing()` injects a REFACTOR comment when `created_map[finding_key]` is set. Source: `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` lines ~443–477; `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` `create_smell_work_item()`.
- Q: "Which branch drops the finding without a report reason?" — Answer (research, agent): The `if not smell_work_item_id:` branch in `remediate_pre_existing()` (generic warning + `comment_errors += 1`), reached whenever `create_smell_work_item()` returns `None` from any guard or a `wl create` failure. Source: `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` lines ~458–464.
- Q: "Are the recorded smells session-introduced or pre-existing?" — Answer (source log, SA-0MVZE164P0048306 finish log): pre-existing (`session_introduced: 0`, `pre_existing: 5`); the item that surfaced this landed green. Source: `/tmp/finish2_SA-0MVZE164P0048306.log`.

# Reduce Large Tool-Call Results Before They Enter Conversation History

## Problem Statement

A single oversized tool-call result (e.g. a 51 KB SKILL.md pasted by the audit skill) inflates the conversation history, causing every subsequent model turn to re-prefill a bloated tail. Measured impact: a 51,945-byte tool message inflated 6,564 to 33,570 tokens across 7 turns, producing 53 s and 72 s time-to-first-byte on a local model measuring 143-303 tok/s prefill. The proxy under-priced the append (173 tokens billed vs. 12,936 measured), making the cost invisible to admission control.

## Users

- **Pi agents**: All agents working with tool results that exceed reasonable sizes (skill bodies, large file reads, JSON dumps) will benefit from automatic result reduction.
- **Operators**: Reduced prefill times mean faster response cycles and lower GPU contention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A measurement report exists ranking tool-result payload size by tool and session, produced by a committed deterministic script (no model calls), with the top offenders named.
- AC2: Each of the five candidate approaches is assessed for (a) bytes/tokens saved, (b) added latency and GPU contention, (c) information-loss risk and recoverability, with a recorded recommendation.
- AC3: At least one non-model mechanism (truncate-with-re-read or reference-instead-of-inline) is prototyped as a Pi extension and validated against a real oversized tool result, with the before/after prompt-token counts recorded.
- AC4: If a small-model compaction path is implemented, it reuses the existing summariser slot (Qwen2.5-7B preset, parallel=1), is benchmarked against the prefill cost it avoids, and includes a documented fallback when the summariser is unavailable.
- AC5: Documentation states the extension's threshold, behaviour and how an agent recovers truncated content, and the result is recorded against the originating LLM-repo prefill-pricing item.

## Impact

Agents experience faster response times when working with tool results, as oversized payloads are automatically reduced before entering conversation history, avoiding 50+ second prefill delays on subsequent turns.

## Constraints

- Compaction must be cheaper than the prefill it avoids. A ~2 s small-model call must avoid 45-90 s of prefill (saving ~13k tokens at 143-303 tok/s).
- Any lossy step must be recoverable — raw payload retained and re-readable via `offset`/`limit` parameters.
- Runs on the same GPU as the workload it protects; competes for capacity, hence the preference for non-model approaches first.
- Must not alter the tool-call contract — agents must still be able to read content they couldn't fit in one call.

## Candidate Approaches (cheapest first)

1. **Measure first** — rank tool results by bytes/tokens across recorded sessions (deterministic script, no model calls).
2. **Truncate with re-read** — Pi extension intercepts oversized tool results, keeps head/tail, preserves raw output on disk with a re-read marker.
3. **Reference instead of inline** — content-address large or repeated payloads (skill bodies, already-read files), substitute a short handle plus preview.
4. **Small-model compaction** — detect oversized tool results, ask a small model (Qwen2.5-7B summariser slot) to compact them. Escalate only when approaches 2 and 3 are insufficient.
5. **Structured projections** — JSON field selection, summary-by-default with details on demand, at the tool level.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `command/pi.mjs` or equivalent — where tool-call results enter the conversation
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` or audit skill scripts — source of one measured oversized payload
- `~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/` — session recordings for measurement analysis
- `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` — session jsonl files for measurement analysis
- Pi extension framework files — for the truncation/reference implementation

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: Five candidate approaches could tempt implementing all of them. Risk: scope expansion. Mitigation: implement one non-model mechanism for AC3; assess all five for AC2; defer small-model compaction unless validated as necessary.
- **Threshold selection**: The truncation threshold (AC3) must be chosen carefully — too aggressive loses useful content, too permissive doesn't solve the problem. Risk: wrong default. Mitigation: measurement report (AC1) informs threshold; make it configurable.
- **Agent confusion**: Agents may not understand truncation markers or how to re-read content. Risk: agent errors. Mitigation: clear documentation (AC5); test with real agent sessions.
- **GPU contention**: Approach 4 (small-model compaction) competes for the same GPU. Risk: compaction takes longer than prefill savings. Mitigation: benchmark against prefill cost (AC4); fallback to no-op when summariser unavailable.
- **Assumption**: Session recordings at `~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/` and `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` are available for measurement analysis. If not accessible, the measurement script (AC1) should gracefully handle this.

## Related Work

- Originating evidence: LLM-repo worklog items LP-0MW0KZUUS002LICZ (prefill pricing) and LP-0MW0KZV5H004Z4UI.
- Session recordings at `~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/` and session jsonl files at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Should this work be implemented in the SorraAgents repo or the LLM proxy repo? — Answer (agent@herdr): The Pi extension prototype should live in SorraAgents (where Pi extensions are managed), but the measurement script and documentation should link back to the LLM-repo prefill-pricing items. Source: intake assessment.
- Q: What threshold should trigger truncation? — Answer (agent@herdr): TBD — the measurement report (AC1) will inform a data-driven threshold. A reasonable starting point for prototyping is 10 KB or ~5,000 tokens. Source: intake assessment, to be confirmed by measurement.
- Q: Should the extension handle both text and binary results? — Answer (agent@herdr): Focus on text-based results (file reads, tool output) for AC3; binary handling can be deferred to implementation. Source: intake assessment.
data.title: Reduce large tool-call results before they enter conversation history

# Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in SorraAgents

## Why

This project's worklog database is behind the installed `wl` version. Every `wl` invocation prints:

```
Worklog: database at /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog/worklog.db has schemaVersion=8 but the application expects schemaVersion=9. Required columns were repaired automatically. see 'wl doctor upgrade' to list and apply pending migrations
```

Required columns are being patched on every invocation instead of migrated, and the git hooks are stale. Discovered during the 2026-11-04 downtime-dispatcher RCA (the same finding exists across the other worklog roots).

## Pending work (from `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`)

### Schema migrations (0)

_None — only hooks below are pending._

### Outdated git hooks

- pre-push, post-checkout, post-merge, post-rewrite, worklog-post-pull

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want this project's worklog schema and git hooks fully up to date, so that `wl` stops auto-patching columns on every call and so every worklog hook behaves like the current template.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` afterwards reports `pending: []` and no hook whose `status` is not `up-to-date`.
2. `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` was executed against this project's database and applied the migrations listed above.
3. A plain `wl list --json` invocation no longer prints the `schemaVersion=8 … expects schemaVersion=9` warning.
4. **Data-safety check.** The count of items with `needsProducerReview == true` is identical before and after:
   `wl list --json | jq '[.workItems[] | select(.needsProducerReview == true)] | length'`
   Record both numbers on this item.
5. `wl doctor` reports no new findings attributable to this upgrade (any residual finding is recorded on a follow-up item, not ignored).
6. The before/after `--dry-run --json` output is recorded in a comment on this item.

## Plan

1. Capture the baseline: `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` plus the `needsProducerReview` count → comment on this item.
2. Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`.
3. Re-run `--dry-run` (expect nothing pending) and re-check the `needsProducerReview` count (must be unchanged).
4. If the upgrade touched tracked files (`.githooks/`, hook templates), commit them following build → test → commit order.

## Risks & notes

- `--confirm` applies migrations **non-interactively, including UNSAFE ones**. Review the `[UNSAFE]` entries above before running. The database is the runtime source of truth (SQLite); never edit `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and never run `wl import` (destructive).
- If the `needsProducerReview` count changes, STOP, restore, and raise a `bug` against ContextHub's `wl` migration set instead of continuing — the drop/re-add cycle is the suspected cause of the permanent schema-8 oscillation.

## Provenance

The implement skill's dev-push block documents the gate as bound to the pushed
commit (`run_tests.py --gate-commit <sha> --project-root <root>`) and as
mirroring the cache from the checkout actually gated. After the canonical
template gained `mirror_suite_cache` (SA-0MW20Y5YI004QS3M) the remaining gap is
the commit binding: `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` still runs the suite unbound. Once
WL-0MW2A3NAP0088IE9 lands, the template delivers the documented contract and
the skill text must describe the final behaviour — including the refusal
semantics and the dirty-checkout impact — as canonical-template behaviour, not
as a repository-local patch.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (step 9 dev-push block) states that the
   commit-bound gate (`--gate-commit` + `--project-root`, multi-commit refusal,
   cache mirrored from the gate-resolved root) is canonical-template behaviour
   delivered by `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT`, and that `.githooks/pre-push` must not
   be patched locally.
2. The refusal semantics are stated: when no clean checkout holds the pushed
   commit the push is refused (exit 2) with the `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` escape
   hatch; `.gitignore`d `.worklog/` churn does not make a checkout dirty.
3. The text names the runner-compatibility behaviour chosen in the template
   (Q1 = (c): an explicit pre-check refusal when the resolved runner predates
   `--gate-commit`, instead of an argparse error).
4. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (docs-only change;
   the docs lint/graph checks and the dev-push gate are the enforcement).

## Constraints

- Prose-only change in the implement skill; no behaviour change in this repo.
- Do not restate the template's shell code; describe the contract.

  behaviour.

  behaviour" is satisfied formally by that edge. See the pre-implementation

template:

```bash
grep -n 'gate-commit' ../ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts
```

# Goal

One-off operational sweep of the stale `<id>.pending-screens.json` signals left behind by the broken in-main-slot resume cycle fixed in SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S, so the affected items stop being constrained by a gate that can no longer clear.

Discovered-from: SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (audit comment 2026-10-29, "Adjacent scope note 2"). Blocked-by SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S — now **completed** (`stage: done`, shipped in v0.1.26), so the sweep is actionable.

## Current state (verified at intake, 2026-11-16)

The backlog recorded on 2026-10-29 no longer exists in the `llm` project:

- The `llm` project is `/home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager` (worklog prefix `LP`); all seven backlogged IDs resolve there.
- **0 `LP-*.pending-screens.json` files remain.** `ls /home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager/.worklog/audit-checkpoints/*.pending-screens.json` → no such file; the `audit-checkpoints/` directory itself is absent.
- **All seven backlogged items are terminal:** each is `status: completed`, `stage: done` — LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI, LP-0MVB8F5ZU0079DE9, LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4, LP-0MVGT0E6W000Q8CY, LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0, LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X, LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG.
- **One closure cleared a signal without servicing it.** LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 is closed (`completed`/`done`) but its stored report still reads `Ready to close: No` with `Child screens pending: 1` naming LP-0MVVETUDF004FWEB; that child is independently `open` (a `test-failure` item). The parent was closed by producer decision rather than by collecting the screen; the outstanding child is tracked on its own item.

Net: for this item's **stated `llm` scope** the sweep is already satisfied — no item is constrained by a stale signal, and all seven backlogged parents are terminal.

## Cross-project inventory (new finding)

The same class of signal still exists in other project worklogs — 43 files across 7 projects (machine scan, 2026-11-16):

| Project | Signals |
|---|---|
| SorraAgents | 13 |
| AI_Hell | 9 |
| tce-the-rising | 5 |
| Tableau-Card-Engine | 5 |
| ContextHub | 5 |
| tce-main-street | 4 |
| ToneForge | 2 |

Some are genuinely pending; others are likely stale leftovers of the runner bug SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU ("audit runner leaves stale pending-screens.json when no child screens remain", open/low), which reports a resume that empties `pending_child_screens` in its payload while leaving the file on disk.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Enumerate every `<id>.pending-screens.json` under each project's `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/` (llm + the 7 projects with signals) and reconcile against the 2026-10-29 table, recording additions/removals in a comment. Intake result: **0 under llm-manager**, 43 across SorraAgents (13), AI_Hell (9), tce-the-rising (5), Tableau-Card-Engine (5), ContextHub (5), tce-main-street (4), ToneForge (2) — recorded as comment evidence.
- AC2: For each remaining signal, run the parent audit once with the D1/D2 fix in place; where the child audits are already serviced the signal clears automatically, otherwise run a forced `--no-child-in-main-slot` audit so child screens execute in the runner instead of being emitted for an absent interactive session.
- AC3: Each affected item's audit state is recorded (report verdict + whether the signal is gone); no signal remains for an item whose children are all audited.
- AC4: The sweep does not change verdicts by hand — `wl audit-set` is never used directly; only real runner audits persist reports.
- AC5: Producer scope decision **Q1 = (b) — widened**. The sweep covers every project worklog enumerated at intake (llm-manager 0, plus 43 signals across 7 other projects); each signal is classified genuine-pending vs stale before any forced re-audit (a forced run re-bills full audit cost).
- AC6 (validation): Validation is evidence-based — signal presence/absence confirmed by filesystem enumeration and `wl audit-show <id> --json`; no verdict is fabricated.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators across all projects stop seeing backlogged items clamped by a `Child screens pending` gate that can no longer clear, and the reconciliation makes explicit that the original seven-item `llm` backlog is already gone while the 43-signal backlog in the other seven projects gets classified and cleared.

## Minimal implementation

- **llm scope (already done at intake):** the reconciliation record — enumerate the (now empty) checkpoint directory, map the seven IDs to their terminal states — is posted as a comment on this item.
- **Widened scope (producer Q1 = (b), 2026-11-16):**
  1. Enumerate every `<project>/.worklog/audit-checkpoints/*.pending-screens.json` across the 7 projects with signals (SorraAgents 13, AI_Hell 9, tce-the-rising 5, Tableau-Card-Engine 5, ContextHub 5, tce-main-street 4, ToneForge 2).
  2. Per signal, classify genuine-pending vs stale from the parent/child audit state via `wl audit-show <id> --json` and the signal's `pending_child_screens` (stale = the pending set is provably empty, or the parent/children are terminal — SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU leftovers; genuine = a parent still has unserviced, non-terminal children).
  3. Per genuinely pending parent, run `python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue <id> --no-child-in-main-slot --force` (or the default mode where a fresh serviced child audit exists) and record log paths + `wl audit-show <id> --json` as evidence.
  4. Record per-item evidence (verdict + signal gone) and the stale/gone classification on this item; never use `wl audit-set`.

## Constraints

- **No fabricated verdicts:** `wl audit-set` is never called directly; only a real runner audit persists a report (AC4).
- **Cost-aware:** a forced `--no-child-in-main-slot` audit re-bills a full audit per item, so classify genuine-pending vs stale before forcing.
- **No manual file surgery beyond a genuine stale cleanup:** deleting a signal is only valid where the pending set is provably empty; otherwise clear it by servicing the children.
- **Operational, not a fix:** this item is a one-off sweep; the root-cause guard against stale leftovers is SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU and stays out of scope here.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope (resolved):** producer chose Q1 = (b) — the cross-project backlog is in scope for this item; no follow-up item needed for the inventory.
- **Cost blow-out if forced blindly:** mitigate by classifying stale vs genuine first (Q1 recommendation).
- **Assumption:** `llm` = `/home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager` (worklog prefix `LP`) — verified by resolving all seven IDs there.
- **Assumption:** a parent closed while its stored report still shows a pending child (LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0) is a producer closure, not evidence that the screen was serviced; the outstanding child is tracked on LP-0MVVETUDF004FWEB.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (read-only — `--force`, `--no-child-in-main-slot`, `_read_pending_screens_signal`/`_write_pending_screens_signal`)
- `<project>/.worklog/audit-checkpoints/*.pending-screens.json` (the sweep target; `llm-manager` currently has none)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` / `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (the documented resume/clear contract)

## Related work

- SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S — parent fix (D1 freshness gate + D2 checkpoint resume); **completed**.
- SA-0MW2J7NGP006CIEG, SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM, SA-0MW2J7OPP007MAPV — the four landed fix slices; **completed**.
- SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU — "audit runner leaves stale pending-screens.json when no child screens remain"; open/low. Root-cause bug for stale leftovers; a sweep is only a workaround.
- SA-0MW2J8G260045D17 — "Dispatched audits should not emit unservicable screens" (adjacent scope note 1); open.
- SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45, SA-0MVZ3SMK6007431I, SA-0MUH6H87Z001HYJ7 — completed child-screen classification / resume behaviour.

## Producer scope decision (Q1 — answered 2026-11-16)

**Q1 — Scope.** The `llm` backlog this item was written against is now empty (no signals, all seven items terminal), while 43 signals remain across seven other projects. Should this item:

- (a) be **closed as already-satisfied** for its stated `llm` scope, with the cross-project inventory recorded on a new follow-up item; or
- (b) be **widened** to sweep all project worklogs — classify each signal genuine-pending vs stale, and run a forced `--no-child-in-main-slot` audit only where a parent still has genuinely unserviced children?

**Producer answer: (b) — widen.** The sweep covers all project worklogs; classify stale vs genuine first, then force `--no-child-in-main-slot` only for genuinely unserviced parents. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-16 (comment on this item).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Note:** the item was seeded with a complete goal, a known-backlog table, four testable ACs, a minimal implementation sketch and Key Files, so no requirement discovery was needed via interview. The single decision below is a genuine scope choice routed to the producer.

- **Q1 — Scope (see decision above).** **Answer (producer): (b)** — widen the sweep to all project worklogs, classifying each signal genuine-pending vs stale and forcing `--no-child-in-main-slot` only where a parent still has genuinely unserviced children. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-16 (recorded in the question comment on this item). Final: (b). Context recorded at intake: llm-manager has no `audit-checkpoints/` directory and zero `pending-screens.json`; all seven backlogged IDs are `completed`/`done`; 43 signals remain in 7 other projects. ## Goal

Decide and implement how non-interactive (herdr-downtime-dispatched) audits avoid the in-main-slot pending-screens trap: a dispatched audit has no interactive invoking session to perform the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens, so by construction every dispatched parent audit lands in the unserviced state.

Discovered-from: SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (audit comment 2026-10-29, "Adjacent scope note 1"). Distinct from the D1/D2 resume defects: even with a working resume cycle, nobody services a dispatched audit's screens.

## Context and Discovery

This item was auto-dispatched by the herdr-downtime worker on 2026-11-17. The root cause is that the in-main-slot mode (introduced in SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE) relies on an interactive agent session to parse and execute `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` markers emitted by the audit runner. When a downtime-dispatched audit runs non-interactively, there is no session to consume these markers, so child screens are effectively lost — the audit hangs in an unserviceable pending state.

## Producer decision (AC1) — runner-side context detection

**Decision (producer, 2026-11-17):** Adopt the **runner-side** approach. The audit runner resolves `child_in_main_slot=False` when it detects it is running in a dispatched / non-interactive context, so child screens execute in isolated `pi` subprocesses with the runner's own parsing and retry — no interactive session required.

**Rejected alternative:** dispatcher-side `--no-child-in-main-slot` flag passed from the herdr downtime worker. Rejected because it only covers one caller: any other non-interactive entry point (cron, CI, future dispatchers) would still emit unserviceable screens. Runner-side detection makes the behaviour a property of the runner, not of each caller.

**Accepted trade-off:** separate-process child audits cost one `pi` subprocess per child (more expensive than in-main-slot), but they need no interactive session and therefore always make progress — strictly better than hanging in the unserviced pending state.

**Resolution precedence (AC4):** explicit `--child-in-main-slot` / `--no-child-in-main-slot` flag > `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` env var > dispatch/non-interactive detection > default `True`. The explicit flag and env var keep their existing absolute precedence, so an operator can always override detection.

**Resolution source must be logged** (e.g. `child_in_main_slot resolved to False (source: dispatch-detection)`) so the chosen mode is traceable in runner output and audit logs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. AC1: The chosen mechanism (runner-side dispatch detection) and the rejected alternative (dispatcher-side flag) are recorded on this item with the rationale and the accepted trade-off — already satisfied by the `## Producer decision (AC1)` section above; the implementation must honour it.
2. AC2: Dispatched audits no longer emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens that nobody services: a dispatched run either completes its child screens itself in isolated `pi` subprocesses or reports a documented, actionable state.
3. AC3: An interactive audit launched from an agent session keeps in-main-slot mode by default — no behaviour change for the interactive path.
4. AC4: Regression coverage proves the resolution precedence (explicit flag > env `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` > dispatch detection > default `true`), with `wl`/`pi` mocked (no real subprocess).
5. AC5: The resolved mode and its source are logged, and the log line is asserted in the regression coverage.

## Implementation notes (runner-side)

- Add a dispatch/non-interactive detector (e.g. an explicit dispatch marker env such as a herdr/downtime-dispatched indicator) consulted inside `_resolve_child_in_main_slot()` after the CLI flag and `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` env var.
- Return the resolution source alongside the boolean so the caller can log it; keep the helper backward-compatible for existing callers (or add a sibling helper returning `(value, source)`).
- Emit one clear log line at resolution time naming the source; on the dispatched path the runner must not emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]`.
- Ensure the downtime worker sets the dispatch marker (or the runner can otherwise identify a non-interactive context) — confirm the marker's origin during implementation and record it in a comment.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_child_in_main_slot`, `cmd_issue` child-mode resolution, logging of the resolution source
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — `TestChildInMainSlotGateResolution` (extend with dispatch-detection precedence cases)
- herdr downtime worker dispatch path — must set the dispatch marker; locate before editing

## Dependencies

- Related to SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (its resume fixes are a prerequisite for any in-main-slot dispatch to be recoverable, but this item is not blocked by it).
- Related to SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS (Sweep stale in-main-slot pending-screens signals) — adjacent scope.

## Deliverables

- Runner-side dispatch detection with logged resolution source + regression tests.

## Impact

Downtime-dispatched audits now finish their own child screens instead of stalling in a pending state that nobody services, so overnight audit runs produce verdicts without human intervention.

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- **Q:** Which mechanism should be adopted — dispatcher-side `--no-child-in-main-slot` flag, or runner-side dispatch/context detection? — **Answer (producer):** Option 2, runner-side context detection. Source: interactive reply on 2026-11-17 ("2"). Rationale recorded above: covers every non-interactive entry point, not just the herdr downtime worker. No further questions; no prior answer changed.

- **Q:** Which env var should the herdr downtime worker set for dispatch detection — a new `HERDR_DOWNTIME=1` marker (recommended) or the existing `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT=false`? — **Answer (producer):** Option 1, `HERDR_DOWNTIME=1`. Source: interactive reply on 2026-11-17 ("Option 1"). Rationale: it keeps the detection tier meaningful (source `dispatch-detection` stays reachable and assertable, as AC5 requires), keeps the caller declaring *context* while the runner decides *mode*, and does not overload the documented operator-override env var with a third meaning. Reusing `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT=false` would collapse the dispatch tier into the `env` tier and re-create the rejected dispatcher-side coupling one layer down. Prior recommendation in the same session: `HERDR_DOWNTIME=1` (unchanged; no answer revised). Watch item recorded: the marker is emitted from ContentCreator's herdr dispatch path, which cannot be edited from this repository's worktree — tracked as child SA-0MWL51XNM001HMVC (cross-repo hand-off).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MU32TE120012T49** – R5: Enforce the child-audit execution contract (no silent pending child screens) (completed)
- **SA-0MVAWFQ4A002XCAO** – Interactive audit regression guard (completed)
- **SA-0MVAWFPVU001E1T0** – Unserviced in-main-slot verdict tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mt2xrgeu0009qre, 0mvstz71j001p67s, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+147 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+146 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+146 more)
