# Investigate a lingering `implement` assignee left on a completed driven child

## Observation

Child `WL-0MWJE9N7L001V6XI` (ContextHub) was implemented by a driven session
(headless `pi -p "/skill:implement ..."`) spawned by `implement.py drive`. It
reached `completed` / `in_review` with commit `691cbecdc`, its terminal
transition and 'Implementation complete.' comment were written at
2026-11-25T23:54:17Z, and the driver removed its worktree and continued to the
next child.

That item's `updatedAt` later moved to 2026-11-26T00:21:54Z (about 27 min
after the terminal write) with **no accompanying comment**, and the item was
left carrying a non-empty `assignee` of `implement`. Its sibling children
(`WL-0MWJE9J2Y001VZ1M`, `WL-0MWJE9IEH001R3P1`, `WL-0MWJE9MIR005SBQK`) all ended
with an empty assignee, so the release worked for them.

A non-empty assignee is a scheduling hold, so the claim was cleared by hand
(`wl update WL-0MWJE9N7L001V6XI --assignee "" --if-assignee implement`); the
work itself was unaffected.

## Root cause — confirmed (2026-11-27)

The later writer was neither `implement.py` (`phase_finish` / `phase_drive` /
`phase_parent` / `_finalise_stranded_child`) nor the downtime dispatcher. It was
the **`wl sync` merge resolver** in the `wl` CLI
(`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/sync/field-merge.ts`,
`mergeDifferentTimestampItems()`).

Evidence — `ContextHub/.worklog/logs/sync.log.1`, sync round resolved at
2026-11-26T00:18:23Z (the observed `updatedAt` 00:21:54Z follows it):

```
Conflict item=WL-0MWJE9N7L001V6XI ... type=different-timestamp
  local=2026-11-25T23:54:18.399Z remote=2026-11-26T00:18:23.462Z
  field=status   chosen=local  reason=local has completed status (close) local="completed" remote="in-progress" chosen="completed"
  field=sortIndex chosen=remote reason=remote is newer (2026-11-26T00:18:23.462Z) local=600 remote=800 chosen=800
  field=assignee chosen=remote reason=remote is newer (2026-11-26T00:18:23.462Z) local="" remote="implement" chosen="implement"
  field=stage    chosen=local  reason=local has done stage (close) local="in_review" remote="intake_complete" chosen="in_review"
```

The merge resolved the **close** in favour of the local side for `status` and
`stage`, but `assignee` fell through to the generic default-vs-value /
newest-wins rule, so the losing side's non-empty claim was resurrected onto an
item the *same merge* had just marked `completed` / `in_review`. A merge writes
no comment, which explains the comment-less `updatedAt` bump. The
`restoreSide` guard (WL-0MWMRNL2W003W5R3) covers only restore-versus-tombstone
pairs, so it does not apply here. The sibling children were unaffected because
their records were not in conflict in that round.

Not the merge field policy: WL-0MV85WBZ2004VDUQ deliberately made `assignee` an
ordinary merge field so a cleared `""` propagates. The defect is
*intra-record incoherence* — a terminal status paired with the losing side's
live claim — not the field policy. WL-0MWUSJTZN000MXTF is the same class of
defect in the tombstone direction.

## Scope

- **Owning fix (cross-repo):** `src/sync/field-merge.ts` in the ContextHub repo
  (`wl` CLI). It cannot be built, tested or worktreed from this repository, so
  it is tracked as a cross-repo item (see the plan child below) rather than
  implemented here.
- **This repository:** a post-sync defensive backstop (a terminal item can never
  keep a claim), regression tests and documentation, per the assignee-release
  invariant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The merge-conflict root cause is recorded and cited by the cross-repo merge
      item.
- [ ] A terminal-claim repair releases an assignee on a completed item
      regardless of claim age, idempotently, with a comment naming the previous
      assignee.
- [ ] The terminal-claim repair never clears needsProducerReview, the only
      persistent hold.
- [ ] A regression test proves a completed item's claim is released and a
      non-terminal claim untouched.
- [ ] A test proves the post-sync hook runs the terminal-claim repair after a
      sync.
- [ ] docs/dev/assignee-release.md documents the merge-resurrection failure mode
      and the repair backstop.
- [ ] A ContextHub work item tracks the merge claim and close coherence fix with
      a failing-first TypeScript test.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/claim_release.py` — `should_release_assignee`, `release_claim`,
  `reap_stale_claims` (the TTL sweep that deliberately skips terminal items).
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` — `sync_worklog()` / `_run_reaper`, the
  post-sync hook the backstop plugs into.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_claim_release.py` — claim-release unit tests.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_worklog_sync.py` — post-sync reaper hook tests.
- `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` — the canonical backstop documentation.
- Cross-repo (ContextHub, not this checkout):
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/sync/field-merge.ts` and its sync
  merge test suite.

## Plan

Vertical slices, test-first:

1. **Test: post-sync backstop releases terminal-item claims** (task, tests) —
   failing-first coverage in `skill/shared/tests/`.
2. **Release terminal-item claims in the post-sync backstop** (task) — the
   `claim_release` helper plus the `worklog_sync` hook.
3. **Document the sync-merge claim resurrection backstop** (docs).
4. **Record the merge claim/close coherence defect in the ContextHub store**
   (task) — the cross-repo tracking item that owns the real fix.

Children 1 → 2 → 3 are dependency-ordered; child 4 is independent and may run
first because it hands the root cause to the owning repository.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which code path wrote `assignee: implement` onto a `completed` item ~27
  min after its terminal transition?" — Answer (agent, research): the `wl sync`
  merge resolver `mergeDifferentTimestampItems()`; close-preservation wins
  `status`/`stage` per field while `assignee` uses newest-wins, resurrecting the
  losing side's claim. Evidence:
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog/logs/sync.log.1` lines
  13826–13831 (round resolved 2026-11-26T00:18:23Z).
- Q: "Does the fix belong in this repository?" — Answer (agent, research +
  documented assumption): no. `wl`'s source is the ContextHub repo; this
  checkout cannot build or worktree it (worktree isolation + repository
  boundary disciplines). Assumption: this repo supplies the defensible backstop
  (invariant enforcement) and a cross-repo item carries the owning fix. Cheap to
  reverse if the producer prefers a single-repo change.
- Q: "Should the backstop replace the TTL reaper?" — Answer (agent, research):
  no. The reaper is TTL-bounded, comment-recording and deliberately skips
  terminal items; the new repair targets terminal items only and reuses
  `should_release_assignee` / `release_claim`. Both are idempotent and
  complementary.
- Q: "Is a producer decision required before implementing the backstop?" —
  Answer (agent): no. The assignee-release invariant already requires a release
  on every terminal outcome; adding a terminal-item backstop enforces the
  documented rule and does not widen the hold model.

Plan: changelog — 2026-11-27: root cause confirmed from the ContextHub sync
conflict log; ACs 2 and 3 of the original description (implement-skill writer /
dispatcher writer) are answered negatively and rewritten into one backstop AC
plus a cross-repo tracking AC; plan children added.

## Impact

A finished work item stops carrying a phantom scheduling hold, so hold
reporting and dispatch decisions reflect reality instead of a stale claim.

## Related work

- **WL-0MWJ7QYX0001KAQX** — the epic whose drive surfaced this
  (`discovered-from`).
- **WL-0MWJE9N7L001V6XI** — the affected child; see its assignee-release
  comment.
- **WL-0MV85WBZ2004VDUQ** — decided `assignee` is an ordinary merge field (the
  policy is preserved by this plan).
- **WL-0MWUSJTZN000MXTF** — the same merge-resurrection class in the tombstone
  direction.
- **WL-0MWMRNL2W003W5R3** — the `restoreSide` guard that covers only
  restore-versus-tombstone pairs.

## Problem statement

## Users

- **AI agents** that load SKILL.md files into their context window at session start.
- **Operators** who need to maintain and understand skill behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every SKILL.md file is reviewed and reduced in size; each child item produces a measurable reduction (target: ≥20% size reduction per item) without removing functional instructions.
2. Duplicated boilerplate (report rendering, tool-output budget, background job etiquette) is extracted to a single shared reference (`skill/shared/`) and each skill references it.
3. All non-essential work-item ID references (SA-0..., AH-0...) are removed from SKILL.md files; traceability is preserved via comments on the parent work item or in the git history, not in the skill docs.
4. Each child item's PR includes a summary report documenting: original size, new size, percentage reduction, sections removed or extracted, and evidence that no functional instruction was lost.
5. The skill-linter is updated to flag near-duplicate boilerplate in SKILL.md files as an automated finding.
6. After all children are implemented, the total SKILL.md token footprint is reduced by at least 25% compared to the pre-change baseline.

# Use the worklog acceptance-criteria table instead of parsing AC prose

## Problem statement

SorraAgents skills recover a work item's acceptance criteria by regexing the
`## Acceptance Criteria` section out of the work item's `description` (canonical
implementation: `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria`).
Worklog is adding a first-class `acceptance_criteria` table with one row per
criterion — stable id, ordering, text, status (`met|unmet|partial|modified`)
and, for `modified` rows, the original text plus the justification. Skills must
switch from prose parsing to the table so a criterion has identity and status.

## Users

- **Pi agent sessions** that run skills consuming acceptance criteria programmatically: `audit`, `implement`, `find-related`, `plan`, `intake`, `report`.
- **Developer** maintaining those skills — needs predictable, testable AC behaviour regardless of description edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every skill that extracts acceptance criteria programmatically reads them from
  the worklog table (`wl ac show <id> --json`) instead of parsing description
  text; `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` either
  delegates to the table or remains only as an explicit legacy/description
  fallback, with the fallback documented and tested.
- `find-related` and `implement` are updated first (as named in the parent
  request) to use the AC rows rather than a full `wl show` where the table
  suffices.
- AC-coverage review (`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::compute_coverage` /
  `apply_coverage_review`) compares criteria rows — by id where both sides are
  migrated, by similarity only for unmigrated descriptions — and its behaviour
  is covered by tests.
- Per-criterion status is honoured where the skills already reason about
  criteria (audit reports, plan coverage, intake briefs): a `met` criterion does
  not count as a gap, and a `modified` criterion is shown with its original text
  and justification.
- Skills remain functional against a store that has **not** yet run `wl doctor
  upgrade` (no AC rows): the fallback path is exercised by a test.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Agents stop re-parsing acceptance criteria out of prose and read them as
addressable rows with their own status, so a criterion can be cited by id and a
re-worded criterion is visibly `modified` rather than silently different.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the Worklog store beyond the existing `wl` CLI surface: no
  writes to the `acceptance_criteria` table from the skills.
- The skills ship from this repository; the table is delivered by ContextHub
  `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG`. Do not implement schema or CLI changes here.
- `AC status is advisory in this phase` (ContextHub decision Q3 = advisory): no
  skill may gate closure on AC status yet — 15,172 back-filled criteria start as
  `unmet`.
- **Blocking dependency**: this work cannot be implemented until the ContextHub
  `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` (Add a table for ACs) delivers the `wl ac` CLI and
  back-fill. That item is `blocked`/`plan_complete`. This item must be marked
  blocked-on that dependency.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` parses prose from
  `## Acceptance Criteria` headings using regex/line-scanning.
- `skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py::run_wl_show` fetches a full
  `wl show` to read descriptions (and indirectly, AC prose).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` extracts AC lines internally and
  supports `adjusted` verdicts in its own vocabulary but does not yet use the
  AC table.
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` accepts `acceptance_criteria` rows
  but only from the render_report CLI, not from skills.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `skill/intake/SKILL.md`
  reference AC coverage via prose-parsed lists.

## Desired change

All skills that programmatically consume ACs delegate to `wl ac show <id> --json`
(or an equivalent table-read helper). Where the AC table is absent (pre-migration
stores), a documented fallback reads prose. AC-coverage comparison uses row ids
when available, falls back to string similarity when not.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Migration window risk:** Both prose-fallback and table-backed code paths must
  coexist during the transition. Any regression in prose-fallback will break
  skills against un-migrated stores.
  *Mitigation:* exhaustive fallback tests before table migration; phased rollout.
- **Scope creep:** All listed skills (tree_coverage, find-related, implement, plan,
  intake, audit, report) in a single change-set is large. Risk of merge conflicts
  and review fatigue.
  *Mitigation:* implement in dependency order (tree_coverage → find-related →
  implement → audit → report → skill docs).
- **Assumption:** the `wl ac show` CLI surface (JSON shape) stabilises before
  implementation begins. If it changes, the table-adapter in tree_coverage will
  need revision.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — needs table-backed AC reads and the
  documented legacy fallback.
- `skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py` — needs AC rows instead of a
  full `wl show` where possible.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — needs the AC workflow to read rows.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — need the coverage/brief
  paths updated.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — needs its per-criterion verdicts
  reconciled with the table's status vocabulary (`adjusted` ≈ `modified`).
- `skill/shared/tests/` — needs coverage tests for table-backed reads plus the
  no-AC-rows fallback.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is the `wl ac` CLI already available in the SorraAgents environment?"

- **SA-0MW6ZZ1HR009DD9Q** – Close coverage gap: **Mode resolution and default.** `audit_runner.py issue` (and `batch`) accepts `--strict` / `--no... (completed)
- **SA-0MP3YN1HH000SCX9** – make success criteria and acceptance criteria synonyms (completed)

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, add, adjusted, agents (+150 more)

## Plan decomposition (plan skill, 2026-11-26T23:42:45Z)

Decomposed into nine child items in dependency order: test-first harness first,
then the shared adapter, the table-aware coverage engine, the named consumers
(`find-related`, `implement`), `audit`, `report`, documentation, and finally the
legacy-store end-to-end regression gate.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |

| 1 | AC table fixtures and fake runner (SA-0MWY74267003UVSD) | task | WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG (foreign) |

## Goal

Stop work items staying `blocked` after every dependency edge they hold is `completed`, so `wl next` can dispatch them.

## Problem

Observed twice on the same leaf (2026-11-18 and 2026-11-26): `SA-0MWJCDH5K002M5H5` (child of SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1) was `blocked` while its only outbound edge `SA-0MWJ7K962006646G` was `completed`. A stale `blocked` hides a ready leaf from `wl next` and from downtime dispatch, so the plan run had to repair the status by hand each time. Something re-derives `blocked` (bulk re-derivation after dependency edits or sync) without re-checking whether the blocking edges are already satisfied.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Reproduction recorded: the code path that sets `blocked` without re-validating completed outbound edges is identified (candidate: bulk status re-derivation in the worklog sync/import path).
2. When every outbound dependency edge of a `blocked` item is `completed`, the item is reconciled to `open` (or its documented ready status) — either at derivation time or by an idempotent sweep — without operator intervention.
3. Items with at least one unmet or missing edge stay `blocked`; `completed`/`deleted` items are never reopened.
4. Targeted tests cover: all-deps-completed `blocked` → reconciled; one-dep-open `blocked` → unchanged; already-`open` item → unchanged (idempotence).
5. Existing adjacent behaviour (SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2 block re-validation at start, SA-0MVUTD408005OFNW skip-blocked classification) keeps passing.

## Impact

Ready leaves stop disappearing from the dispatch queue because of a stale `blocked` status.

# Test: large-parent Phase 2 prompt-size capture contract

## Goal

Pin the prompt-size measurement contract with a deterministic, offline fixture
that reproduces the 2026-11-24 large-parent Phase 2 shape — **before** any
production change lands (TDD).

**User story:** As the release producer, I want a large-parent Phase 2 audit to
report the size of the exact prompt it sent, so a provider error on that shape
can be diagnosed without guessing or a live provider.

## Context / evidence

Parent item `SA-0MWV3N94G007H6A9`. The failing Phase 2 call was on
`RISE-0MW7V58ZP0058NMI`: a parent with 14 children (all `completed`/`done`),
a ~18 KB description and 9 acceptance criteria. The failing runs persisted
`calls=2 parse_ok=1 provider_errors=1` with no prompt size recorded because
`_call_pi` reads `input_tokens` from the `agent_end` usage block, which a
`finish_reason: error` call may not emit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A deterministic offline fixture represents the failing shape: a parent
  with 14+ children carrying persisted audits, a ~18 KB description and 9+
  acceptance criteria. The fixture drives the **production**
  `_run_phase2_deep_analysis` prompt-construction path (the test must not
  re-implement prompt assembly).
- AC2 — A test asserts the measured Phase 2 parent prompt size (bytes and
  estimated tokens) is captured by production code and retrievable from the
  call result / per-call timing line / debug-log entry.
- AC3 — A test asserts the prompt size is still captured on a provider-error
  (`finish_reason: error`) path where the stream carries no `agent_end` usage
  block, so the failing prompt size is never lost.
- AC4 — The tests fail against the current implementation and pass once the
  measurement change (C3) lands, and they run in the audit test suite.
- AC5 — Capture the failure with measured size: the failing Phase 2 prompt shape
  is reproduced deterministically by a fixture (large parent: 14+ children with
  persisted audits, ~18 KB description, 9+ acceptance criteria) with the failing
  prompt's measured size recorded (bytes and estimated tokens), so the size
  hypothesis can be evaluated without a live provider.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/large_parent_phase2.py` building the parent
  dict + 14 child dicts with `ac_results` and persisted-audit markers.
- Add `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase2_prompt_size.py` with tests
  that mock `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` (capturing the real prompt) and assert the
  measured size fields; include the provider-error variant.
- Use the production `_run_phase2_deep_analysis` entrypoint only — no copied
  prompt strings in the test.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/large_parent_phase2.py` (new)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase2_prompt_size.py` (new)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`

## Dependencies

None — this is the first, test-first slice.

## Deliverables

- Deterministic large-parent fixture.
- Failing-then-passing prompt-size capture tests.

## Impact

A large-parent Phase 2 audit will report the exact measured prompt size, so a
provider error can be diagnosed from the log alone instead of guessing.

## Summary

Make `audit_runner.py issue <id>` strictly single-item by default: the post-audit batch drain runs **only** when the operator passes `--batch-drain`. `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN` no longer switches the drain on (it loses its "auto-on" meaning) and `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=0` remains a hard disable of an explicitly requested drain. The audited item's own children keep their current in-scope behaviour.

This is the primary behaviour fix for parent `SA-0MWWE4OI1006OC42` (desired change 1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `audit_runner.py issue <id>` audits **only** `<id>` (and, unchanged, its children): with two or more foreign entries queued in the `audit-batch` queue, a default `cmd_issue` invocation calls neither `_maybe_run_batch_drain` nor `_batch_drain_cycle`, audits none of them, leaves every entry queued, and its exit code and persisted verdict are identical to a run against an empty queue.
- The post-audit drain is **explicit** for `issue`: it runs only when the operator passes `--batch-drain`; neither the default invocation (`batch_drain=None`) nor `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN` set to any value other than `0` can trigger it.
- `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=0` still disables an explicitly requested `--batch-drain` run (hard disable preserved), and `--no-batch-drain` keeps the drain off.
- `_batch_audit_one` continues to pass `batch_drain=False` so a drain can never recurse.
- Regression tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_batch_drain.py` cover default-off, the `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN` semantics matrix, and exit-code/verdict invariance, and pass together with the existing batch-drain suite.

## Minimal Implementation

- Change the `cmd_issue` tail trigger (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~18681) from `batch_drain is not False` to `batch_drain is True`, still gated on `_batch_drain_enabled()`.
- Redefine `_batch_drain_enabled()` (~5722) as a pure hard-disable check: `os.environ.get(AUDIT_BATCH_DISABLE_ENV, "1") != "0"` stays, but its docstring and the surrounding constants must state it is only an opt-out for an explicit request, never a trigger.
- Update the `cmd_issue` docstring (`*batch_drain*` paragraph, ~18321), the `--batch-drain` help text (~19288) and the `--no-batch-drain` help text to describe the new default.
- Tests: default invocation does not call `_maybe_run_batch_drain`; `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=1`/unset does not enable it; `=0` blocks an explicit request; two foreign queued entries leave `queue_remaining` unchanged and the primary verdict/exit code identical.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `cmd_issue` tail trigger (~18681), `_maybe_run_batch_drain` (~18690), `_batch_drain_enabled` (~5722), CLI flags (~19288), `cmd_issue` docstring (~18321).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_batch_drain.py` — existing `_fake_context`, `_enqueue_with_root`, `_recording_audit_one` helpers; extend for default-off and env-matrix coverage.

## Deliverables

- Code change making the `issue` drain explicit opt-in.
- Updated docstrings and CLI help text.
- Unit/regression tests proving default-off and env semantics.

## Constraints

- Do not touch `cmd_batch` (child `SA-…` project-scoped drain item owns scoping; the `batch` subcommand stays the cross-project entry point).
- Children of the audited item remain in scope exactly as today (`--audit-children`, in-main-slot child screens unaffected).
- Behaviour change must be documented loudly: operators may currently rely on the implicit drain; migration path is `audit_runner.py batch`.

## Risky assumptions

- The external herdr dispatcher does not depend on `issue` auto-drain; in-repo research found no dependency and docs present `batch` as the production drain. Recorded in the parent's Risks section.

## TDD

Write the failing test(s) first (default invocation must not drain; `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=1` must not enable), then make them pass.

## Impact

A release-gate or agent audit of one item finishes auditing that item and stops, so its duration and verdict no longer depend on other projects' queued work.

# Red-first regression tests for session-persisted child verdicts

## Goal

Add the failing-before-fix regression tests that pin the behaviours required by the parent item's AC5, so the two runner changes (children of this plan: *Reuse session-persisted child verdicts* and *Never clobber a serviced child audit*) are driven by red-first evidence rather than back-filled after the fix.

Part of parent `SA-0MWWE4XQ8005WM3C`.

## Context (measured 2026-11-26, worklog 1.1.0)

- `wl audit-set --audit-file <report>` **does** store a schema-2 content fingerprint — in the audit record (`wl audit-show --json` → `audit.fingerprint`), computed by `wl` from the item's current title+description (`dist/commands/audit-result.js`, WL-0MVK01BBD005V7KK). It does **not** embed an `Audit content fingerprint (v2):` line in the report text.
- It also sets `workitems.updatedAt = auditedAt` in the same transaction (`dist/persistent-store.js::saveAuditResult`).
- Verified on the reproduction child `SA-0MWFFXNNM00148IX`: stored `fingerprint` equals the current `_compute_content_fingerprint` (`a37400a8…`); `_extract_content_fingerprint(rawOutput)` is `None`; `auditedAt` is `2026-11-25T17:21:08Z` while `updatedAt` is `2026-11-25T22:34:46Z` (a later comment), so the legacy time gate **rejects** the report as stale.
- Consequence for the tests: a time-gate-only fixture would pass while the real reproduction still fails. Fixtures must model the `wl audit-set` storage shape (audit record carries `fingerprint`, report text does not) as well as the fully fingerprint-less older-`wl` shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC5 — Regression tests.** Unit tests cover: (a) a session-persisted, fingerprint-less `wl audit-set` report (`Ready to close: Yes` + AC table) is reused by the gap-mapped path with zero child screens; (b) the persist-overwrite guard skips a pending child report over such a serviced audit; (c) the documented persist command produces a report the reuse path accepts. No real `pi` or `audit_runner` subprocess is invoked.
- Tests are authored first and recorded as **red** on the unfixed runner: an evidence comment on this item names the failing test ids and their assertion messages, before any production change lands.
- Fixtures cover the `wl audit-set` storage shape (audit record `fingerprint` present, no embedded report line, `updatedAt` later than `auditedAt` after a post-persist comment) and the older fully fingerprint-less shape.
- Negative controls are included: a stale serviced audit (content changed) is still re-screened, and `--force` still re-screens.

## Minimal Implementation

- New module `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_session_persisted_child_verdict.py`, reusing the mocked-runner pattern of `TestGapMappedChildAuditReuse` in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` (`audit-show`, `show --children`, `_persist_child_audit` capture; no `pi`).
- Cases: (a) gap-mapped reuse adopts the serviced verdict with `reused_from` + `child_audit_ready` and emits no `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]`; (b) the persist loop makes no `_persist_child_audit` call for the serviced child; (c) a report produced by the documented `wl audit-set` shape is accepted by `_get_child_content_fresh_verdict`.
- Record the red-first evidence as a comment on this item.

## Constraints

- Tests only — no production-code change in this item.
- No real `pi`/`audit_runner` subprocess; `mock.MagicMock()` runner only.
- Do not soften the existing content-fingerprint contract in fixtures (they must include a genuine schema-2 fingerprint value, not a stub string).

## Target outcome

A red test module that fails only for the reasons the parent item describes, and never for fixture artefacts.

## Definition of done

- New test module collects and the intended cases fail on the unfixed tree with assertion messages that name the missing behaviour.
- `run_tests.py --scope changed --group audit` (test skill) run is recorded with the red result.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_session_persisted_child_verdict.py` (new)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` (existing fixture pattern to follow)

## Deliverables

- New regression test module with the three parent-AC5 cases plus negative controls.
- Red-first evidence comment with failing test ids and assertion messages.

## Dependencies

None — this is the test-first item the other plan children depend on.

# Goal

As an agent finishing a work item, I want regression tests that prove a concurrent session's transient churn in the main checkout cannot abort my finish or fail my suite, while a mutation I caused — or one the suite caused in a guarded checkout — still fails, so the fix cannot silently regress into the reported incident.

# Context

- Today `implement.py::_main_checkout_guard_violations` treats *any* path that becomes dirty in the main checkout between the Step-0.75 baseline and a verify point as offending, including a foreign session's `??` untracked creation. `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py::test_violations_report_new_untracked_path` (line 85) pins that as intended, so the reported incident still reproduces one step later than the pre-lock suite gate: the `pre_push` verify aborts, the item is released to `open`, and an already-green suite is discarded.

No real sleeps: use the existing hook/fixture seams.
- AC3 (finish half, present-at-verify variant): a second scripted case leaves the foreign untracked file present at the final verify and asserts the run still completes with the suite's verdict and records the path as excluded evidence.

## Goal

Land a RED-pinned regression test proving that a `blocked` item whose outbound dependency edges are all terminal keeps `blocked` after a store import — the defect observed twice on the same leaf (SA-0MWJCDH5K002M5H5, 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-26: `blocked` while its only edge SA-0MWJ7K962006646G was `completed`).

## Reproduction recorded (parent AC1 evidence)

- **Code path that re-derives `blocked` without re-validation:** `importWorkItems()` and `upsertItems()` in `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts` write every incoming `WorkItem` verbatim through `ctx.store.saveWorkItem(toSave)` and write the dependency edges in the same transaction, but never re-derive `blocked` from the resulting graph. `wl sync` persists its merge result through exactly these two calls (`src/commands/sync.ts`, the `db.upsertItems(...)` / `db.import(...)` call sites).
- **Contrast — why only sync/import shows the defect:** the interactive write paths (`db.update`, `db.deleteSingle` in `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts`) call `reconcileDependentStatus` / `reconcileDependentsForTarget` after a status or stage change. A remote snapshot that still carries `blocked` therefore lands unreconciled.
- **Why existing coverage misses it:** `tests/regression-auto-unblock.test.ts` exercises only the in-process `db.update` path (`db.addDependencyEdge` + `db.update(blocker, {status:'completed'})`), so it can never fail on this defect.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New file `tests/sync-stale-blocked.test.ts` builds a temp store (existing `tests/test-utils.ts` helpers) with a `completed` blocker and a dependent carrying `blocked`, then persists a snapshot that still carries the dependent as `blocked`.
2. Case A — full import: `db.import(items, edges)` keeps the dependent `blocked` today; the pin asserts the persisted status should be `open`.
3. Case B — incremental sync: `db.upsertItems(items, edges)` keeps the dependent `blocked` today; the pin asserts `open`.
4. Both pins use the repository RED-pin convention (`it.fails(...)`) so the configured suite stays green until the implementation child flips them; each pin asserts the concrete persisted status, never merely "did not throw".
5. The identified code path and the reproduction steps are recorded in this item's completion comment, with file paths and line-level references.

6. Parent AC1 — reproduction recorded: the code path that sets `blocked` without re-validating completed outbound edges is identified (the worklog sync/import bulk status re-derivation path in `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts`).

## Key Files

- tests/sync-stale-blocked.test.ts
- packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts
- src/commands/sync.ts

## Notes

- Test-first: this item lands before the implementation child; the pins stay `it.fails` until then.
- Do not weaken or delete any existing assertion in `tests/regression-auto-unblock.test.ts`.

## Implementation location

The `wl` CLI source lives in the ContextHub repository (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`); this work item is tracked here. Follow the established cross-repo pattern (SA-0MSC0BM1V0032UYT landed as an `SA-…` commit in ContextHub): run the implement session from the ContextHub checkout while pointing `wl` at this store via `wl --worklog-dir /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog`.

## Goal

Pin the full behavioural contract of blocked-status reconciliation across the import/upsert paths, so the implementation child has an unambiguous, executable definition of done.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Contract matrix added to `tests/sync-stale-blocked.test.ts` (built on the reproduction fixtures from the first child), each case RED-pinned with `it.fails` while the fix is pending:
   - all outbound edges terminal (`completed`, `deleted`, `in_review`, `done` stage) → `blocked` becomes `open`;
   - at least one active outbound edge → stays `blocked`;
   - `blocked` item with **no** outbound edges (deliberate producer hold) → unchanged (fail closed, consistent with SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2 AC4);

## Goal

Make `wl sync` / `wl import` self-healing: after the incoming snapshot and its dependency edges are written, re-derive `blocked` from the resulting graph so a stale `blocked` is reconciled to `open` without operator intervention (parent AC2), while every genuinely blocked item and every deliberate hold stays blocked (parent AC3).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `reconcileStaleBlockedItems(ctx, ids?)` to `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` (same module as `reconcileBlockedStatus` / `hasActiveBlockers`):
   - candidates: local items with `status === 'blocked'`, not soft-deleted, and with **at least one** outbound dependency edge;
   - unblock a candidate only when `hasActiveBlockers(ctx, id)` is false — reuse the existing predicate and `isDependencyActive` (never fork the terminal rule, so `in_review`/`done` keep their documented meaning);
   - persist via `ctx.store.saveWorkItem` plus `upsertFtsEntry` when FTS is available, and keep the existing `WL_DEBUG` diagnostic style;
   - a `blocked` item with no outbound edges is a deliberate hold and is returned untouched (fail closed).
2. Call the sweep from `importWorkItems()` and `upsertItems()` (both in `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts`) **after** the item/edge transaction completes, scoped to the affected ids — no full-store rebuild, no per-item `triggerAutoSync` storm (one coalesced `triggerAutoSync` for the whole sweep, or none when nothing changed).
3. Expose a thin façade delegate on `WorklogDatabase` (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`) so non-import callers can reuse the sweep.
4. Flip the `it.fails` pins from the two test children to plain `it(...)`.
5. Record the observed defect and the fix location in the completion comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Full import (`db.import`) and incremental sync (`db.upsertItems`) both reconcile a `blocked` dependent whose outbound edges are all terminal to `open`; the first sync after the fix repairs pre-existing stale rows with no operator action.
2. An item with one active outbound edge stays `blocked`; a `blocked` item with no outbound edges is unchanged; `completed`/`deleted` items are never reopened.
3. The sweep performs no writes when nothing needs reconciling (a second run is a no-op, `updatedAt` unchanged) and triggers at most one auto-sync per import.
4. All pins from the test children pass as plain `it(...)`; existing suites `tests/regression-auto-unblock.test.ts`, `tests/regression-explicit-blocked-status.test.ts`, `tests/database-dependencies-import.test.ts` stay green.
5. Cost stays bounded: the sweep inspects only `blocked` candidates in the affected id set, not the whole store.

6. Parent AC2 — when every outbound dependency edge of a `blocked` item is `completed`, the item is reconciled to `open` (or its documented ready status) by the idempotent reconciling sweep in the import/upsert derivation path, without operator intervention.

## Key Files

- packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts
- packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts
- packages/shared/src/database.ts

- Reuse `hasActiveBlockers`/`isDependencyActive` — a second terminal rule is a defect, not an implementation detail.

# Test: post-sync backstop releases terminal-item claims

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want proof that a non-empty `assignee` resurrected onto a
`completed` / `in_review` work item by a `wl sync` merge conflict is released
by the post-sync backstop, so a finished item can never keep a phantom
scheduling hold.

## Background

Parent SA-0MWWUI0KD008U3UN confirmed the writer of the stray claim was
`mergeDifferentTimestampItems()` in the `wl` CLI
(`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/sync/field-merge.ts`): the merge keeps
the local close for `status` / `stage` but takes the *losing* side's non-empty
`assignee`, producing a terminal item with a live claim and no comment.
Evidence: `ContextHub/.worklog/logs/sync.log.1` lines 13826–13831.

The owning fix lands in the ContextHub repository. This item provides the
failing-first coverage for the in-repo defence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A regression test proves a completed item's claim is released and a
      non-terminal claim untouched.
- [ ] A test proves a `completed` / `in_review` item carrying a freshly
      written non-empty `assignee` (claim age well inside the reaper TTL) is
      released by the terminal-claim repair, with a comment naming the
      previous assignee.
- [ ] A test proves a claim on a non-terminal (`in-progress` / `open`) item is
      left untouched by the terminal-claim repair.
- [ ] A test proves `needsProducerReview: true` survives the repair — the flag
      is preserved and is still the only persistent hold.
- [ ] A test proves the repair is idempotent (a second pass is a no-op) and
      that `dry_run` writes nothing.
- [ ] A test proves the post-sync hook runs the terminal-claim repair after a
      sync, and that a repair failure never fails `sync_worklog()`.
- [ ] Every test exercises production code — no re-implementation of the merge
      or repair logic inside the test — and each test fails before the
      implementation item lands.

## Constraints

- Tests only: do not change `skill/shared/claim_release.py` or
  `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` behaviour here (the implementation child owns
  that).
- Route test execution through the test skill (`/skill:test`); never invoke
  pytest directly.
- Reuse the existing `runner=` / `now=` injection seams already used by the
  reaper tests so the suite stays hermetic.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_claim_release.py`
- `skill/shared/tests/test_worklog_sync.py`
- `skill/shared/claim_release.py` (API under test)
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` (post-sync hook under test)

Failing-first tests ready for the implementation child, plus a short note in
the completion comment recording the observed red state.

# ruff ISC004 in test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py:297 — candidate false positive

## Problem statement

Ruff flags ISC004 (Unparenthesized implicit string concatenation in collection) at line 297 of `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py`. The code uses intentional implicit string concatenation to build a single multi-line string; there is no missing comma and the code is correct.

## Users

- Developer running `ruff check` — the finding adds noise to the lint output.
- Audit system — the finding generates a chore work item requiring producer review.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Producer decides: waive ISC004 for this line, or fix the code pattern.
2. If waived, `audit_waiver.py add` records the waiver on this work item.
3. If fixed, `ruff check --isolated --select ISC004 skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py` reports zero findings.
4. All existing tests in `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py` continue to pass.

## Impact

Narrow style-lint noise reduction for a single test-line — no user-visible impact.

## Constraints

- The test expects a single-element list (uses `notes[0]`); adding a comma would break the test by creating a two-element list.
- The broader codebase has ~15 ISC004 findings across multiple files.

## Existing state

```python
    notes = [
        "excluded: concurrently resolved working-tree change in "
        f"{repo}: src/app.ts [ M]"
    ]
```

Two adjacent string literals (one regular, one f-string) inside a list — Python implicitly concatenates them into a single string.

## Desired change

**Option A — Waive the finding:** Accept this as a false positive. The code is correct; ISC004 is a style flag that does not indicate a defect. Add an audit waiver.

**Option B — Fix the code:** Parenthesise the concatenated entry to satisfy ruff:
```python
    notes = [
        (
            "excluded: concurrently resolved working-tree change in "
            f"{repo}: src/app.ts [ M]"
        )
    ]
```

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py` — lines 296–297: the flagged code.

## Related work

- SA-0MWMQC848004Z3XC — "Parenthesise render_summary() list entries to resolve ISC004" (producer chose Option B: fix in code).
- SA-0MWB1AYW0003DKQR, SA-0MWNPTFRT000JYSK, SA-0MWB8VZKO0050NZE, SA-0MWMOCL1Y004I9OR — sibling ISC004 false-positive candidates.
- ~15 total ISC004 findings across the codebase.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Waiver risk:** if the producer chooses waivers, individual work items persist; the underlying style pattern remains unfixed elsewhere.
- **Fix risk:** parenthesising changes the AST slightly but preserves semantics and runtime behaviour; no test change needed.
- **Assumption:** the implicit concatenation is intentional, not a missing-comma bug. Verified by reading the full code context and the test assertions.

## Appendix

### Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should we waive ISC004 for this line (Option A) or parenthesise the concatenated entry to fix the pattern (Option B)?" — Status: **OPEN — awaiting producer decision.**
  - Context: The code is functionally correct; ISC004 is a style-only flag. Precedent: SA-0MWMQC848004Z3XC chose Option B (parenthesise). This is a genuine producer decision per the interview conduct contract.

# Problem

`apply_pane_status()` / `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py:derive_status()` derive the herdr pane title from the **session's own** acceptance criteria only. An audit session whose work item's audit failed can therefore still show a success pane status (done/note), even though SA-0MWIIOMY10054VJI fixed the report Conclusion to render `🚫 Not ready to ship`.

This was flagged in SA-0MWIIOMY10054VJI ("Related surface (consider, not required)") and filed separately because it needs a signature change to `derive_status`/`apply_pane_status`, not a one-line follow-on.

# Desired behaviour

1. For `--skill-name audit`, the pane status is gated on the resolved audit verdict: audit `no`/`unknown` ⇒ `attention`, regardless of session ACs.
2. Non-audit skills are unchanged.
3. Both the CLI `--json` and `render_from_wl` paths pass the verdict through.

# Key files

- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — `derive_status`
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — `apply_pane_status` (already computes `audit_verdict`)

# Acceptance criteria

1. An audit report with `readyToClose: false` sets the pane status to `attention`.
2. An audit report with a missing audit sets the pane status to `attention`.
3. A passing audit keeps today's status derivation.
4. Non-audit skills are unchanged.
5. Tests pass through the test skill and the full suite is green.

# Impact

An operator watching the herdr pane grid can no longer see a green 'done' pane title for an audit session whose audit actually failed.
